Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are navigating in a narrow channel and must remain in the channel for safe operation. Another vessel is crossing the channel ahead of you from your starboard and you doubt whether your vessel will pass safely. Which  statement is TRUE?
Option_A: You must stop your vessel, since the other vessel is the stand-on.
Option_B: You must sound one short blast of the whistle and turn to starboard.
Option_C: You must sound the danger signal.
Option_D: You must stop your engines and you may sound the danger  signal.
Correct_Answer: You must sound the danger signal.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY What is the required whistle signal for a  power-driven vessel leaving a dock or berth?
Option_A: One short blast
Option_B: One prolonged blast
Option_C: Two short blasts
Correct_Answer: One prolonged blast

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY In a narrow channel, you are underway on vessel "A" and desire to overtake vessel "B". After you sound two short blasts on your whistle, vessel "B" sounds five short and rapid blasts on the whistle. You should _________.
Option_A: pass with caution on the port side of vessel "B"
Option_B: hold your relative position, and then sound another signal after the situation has stabilized
Option_C: answer the five short blast signal then stop your vessel until the other vessel initiates a signal
Option_D: slow or stop and expect radical maneuvers from "B"
Correct_Answer: hold your relative position, and then sound another signal after the situation has stabilized

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A vessel proceeding downstream in a narrow  channel on the Western Rivers sights another vessel moving upstream. Which vessel has the right of way?
Option_A: The vessel moving upstream against the current
Option_B: The vessel moving downstream with a following current
Option_C: The vessel located more towards the channel centerline
Option_D: The vessel sounding the first whistle signal
Correct_Answer: The vessel moving downstream with a following current

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are overtaking a power-driven vessel in a narrow channel and wish to leave her on your starboard side. You may  ___________________.
Option_A: attempt to contact her on the radiotelephone to arrange for the passage
Option_B: proceed to overtake her without sounding whistle signals
Option_C: sound five short blasts
Correct_Answer: attempt to contact her on the radiotelephone to arrange for the passage

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A vessel displaying a flashing blue light is _________________.
Option_A: transferring dangerous cargo
Option_B: a law enforcement vessel
Option_C: a work boat
Correct_Answer: a law enforcement vessel

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY When power-driven vessels are crossing, a signal of one short blast by either vessel means _____.
Option_A: "I intend to leave you on my port side"
Option_B: "I intend to hold course and speed"
Option_C: "I intend to change course to starboard"
Option_D: "I request a departure from the Rules"
Correct_Answer: "I intend to leave you on my port side"

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY If you were coming up on another power-driven vessel from dead astern and desired to overtake on the other vessel's starboard side, which whistle signal would you sound?
Option_A: One short blast
Option_B: One prolonged blast
Option_C: Two short blasts
Correct_Answer: One short blast

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which statement is TRUE concerning narrow  channels?
Option_A: You should keep to that side of the channel which is on your port side.
Option_B: You should avoid anchoring in a narrow channel.
Option_C: A vessel having a following current will propose the manner of passage in any case where two vessels are meeting.
Correct_Answer: You should avoid anchoring in a narrow channel.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which term is NOT defined in the Inland   Navigation Rules?
Option_A: Seaplane
Option_B: Restricted visibility
Option_C: Underway
Correct_Answer: Vessel constrained by her draft

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY When you are overtaking another vessel and  desire to pass on her left or port hand, you should sound _________________.
Option_A: one short blast
Option_B: one long blast
Option_C: two short blasts
Correct_Answer: two short blasts

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Your vessel is meeting another vessel head-on. To comply with the steering and sailing rules, you should _____.
Option_A: sound the danger signal
Option_B: sound one prolonged and two short blasts
Option_C: exchange two short blasts
Correct_Answer: exchange one short blast

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Yellow lights are NOT used to identify ________.
Option_A: U.S. submarines
Option_B: vessels pushing ahead
Option_C: law enforcement vessels
Correct_Answer: law enforcement vessels

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You have made your vessel up to a tow and are moving from a pier out into the main channel. Your engines are turning ahead. What whistle signal should you sound?
Option_A: One prolonged and two short blasts
Option_B: Three long blasts
Option_C: One prolonged blast
Option_D: Five or more short rapid blasts
Correct_Answer: One prolonged blast

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Under the Inland Navigation Rules, what is the meaning of the two short blasts signal used when meeting another vessel?
Option_A: "I am turning to starboard."
Option_B: "I am turning to port."
Option_C: "I intend to leave you on my starboard side."
Option_D: "I intend to leave you on my port side."
Correct_Answer: "I intend to leave you on my starboard side."

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY For the purpose of the Inland Navigation Rules, the term "Inland Waters" includes ___________________.
Option_A: the Western Rivers
Option_B: the Great Lakes on the United States side of the   International Boundary
Option_C: harbors and rivers shoreward of the COLREGS demarcation  lines
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A power-driven vessel crossing a river on the Western Rivers has the right of way over ____________________.
Option_A: vessels ascending the river
Option_B: vessels descending the river
Option_C: all vessels ascending and descending the river
Correct_Answer: None of the above

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which lights are required for a barge, not part of a composite unit, being pushed ahead?
Option_A: Sidelights and a sternlight
Option_B: Sidelights, a special flashing light, and a sternlight
Option_C: Sidelights and a special flashing light
Option_D: Sidelights, a towing light, and a sternlight
Correct_Answer: Sidelights and a special flashing light

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A power-driven vessel operating in a narrow  channel with a following current on the Great Lakes or  Western Rivers is meeting an upbound vessel. Which   statement is TRUE?
Option_A: The downbound vessel has the right-of-way.
Option_B: The downbound vessel must initiate the required maneuvering signals.
Option_C: The downbound vessel must propose the manner and place of passage.
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Your vessel is proceeding down a channel, and can safely navigate only within the channel. Another vessel is crossing your bow from port to starboard, and you are in doubt as to her intentions. Which statement is TRUE?
Option_A: The sounding of the danger signal is optional.
Option_B: The sounding of the danger signal is mandatory.
Option_C: You should sound two short blasts.
Option_D: You should sound one prolonged and two short blasts.
Correct_Answer: The sounding of the danger signal is mandatory.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY The stand-on vessel in a crossing situation  sounds one short blast of the whistle. This means that the vessel _____.
Option_A: intends to hold course and speed
Option_B: is changing course to starboard
Option_C: is changing course to port
Option_D: intends to leave the other on her port side
Correct_Answer: intends to leave the other on her port side

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are crossing the course of another vessel which is to your starboard. You have reached an agreement by radiotelephone to pass astern of the other vessel. You MUST _________________.
Option_A: sound one short blast
Option_B: sound two short blasts
Option_C: change course to starboard
Correct_Answer: None of the above

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Passing signals shall be sounded on inland waters by ________________________.
Option_A: all vessels upon sighting another vessel rounding a bend in the channel
Option_B: towing vessel when meeting another towing vessel on a clear day with a 0.6 mile CPA (Closest Point of Approach)
Option_C: a power-driven vessel when crossing less than half a mile ahead of another power-driven vessel
Correct_Answer: a power-driven vessel when crossing less than half a mile ahead of another power-driven vessel

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY In a narrow channel, a power-driven vessel desiring to overtake another power-driven vessel on the other vessel's starboard side will sound a whistle signal of _________________.
Option_A: one short blast
Option_B: two short blasts
Option_C: two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast
Option_D: two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts
Correct_Answer: one short blast

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A law enforcement boat may display a __________.
Option_A: blue flag
Option_B: flashing blue light
Option_C: flashing red light
Correct_Answer: flashing blue light

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Your vessel is meeting another vessel head-on. To comply with the rules you should exchange _____.
Option_A: one short blast, alter course to port, and pass starboard to starboard
Option_B: one short blast, alter course to starboard, and pass port to port
Option_C: two short blasts, alter course to port, and pass starboard to starboard
Option_D: two short blasts, alter course to starboard, and pass port to port
Correct_Answer: one short blast, alter course to starboard, and pass port to port

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A vessel overtaking another in a narrow channel, and wishing to pass on the other vessel's port side, would sound a whistle signal of _________________.
Option_A: one short blast
Option_B: two short blasts
Option_C: two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast
Option_D: two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts
Correct_Answer: two short blasts

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A fleet of moored barges extends into a   navigable channel. What is the color of the lights on the barges?
Option_A: Red
Option_B: Amber
Option_C: White
Correct_Answer: White

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which signal must a power-driven vessel give, in addition to one prolonged blast, when backing out of a berth with another vessel in sight?
Option_A: 2 short blasts
Option_B: 1 blast
Option_C: 3 short blasts
Correct_Answer: 3 short blasts

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY At night, a light signal consisting of two  flashes by a vessel indicates ____.
Option_A: an intention to communicate over radiotelephone
Option_B: that the vessel is in distress
Option_C: an intention to leave another vessel to port
Option_D: an intention to leave another vessel to starboard
Correct_Answer: an intention to leave another vessel to starboard

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are overtaking a power-driven vessel in a narrow channel and wish to leave her on your starboard side. You may  _____________________.
Option_A: proceed to overtake her without sounding whistle signals
Option_B: attempt to contact her on the radiotelephone to arrange for the passage
Option_C: sound four short blasts
Correct_Answer: attempt to contact her on the radiotelephone to arrange for the passage

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY For the purpose of the Inland Navigation Rules, the term "inland waters" includes _____________________.
Option_A: the Great Lakes on the United States side of the   International Boundary
Option_B: the water surrounding any islands of the United States
Option_C: the coastline of the United States, out to one mile   offshore
Correct_Answer: the Great Lakes on the United States side of the   International Boundary

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A barge more than 50 meters long is required to show how many white anchor lights when anchored in a  Secretary of Transportation approved "special anchorage  area"?
INLAND ONLY Which type of vessel is NOT mentioned in the Inland Navigation Rules?
Option_A: An inconspicuous, partly submerged vessel
Option_B: A seaplane
Option_C: An air-cushion vessel
Option_D: A vessel constrained by her draft
Correct_Answer: A vessel constrained by her draft

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are operating a vessel through a narrow  channel and your vessel must stay within the channel to be navigated safely. Another vessel is crossing your course from starboard to port, and you are in doubt as to her  intentions. You _______________________.
Option_A: must sound the danger signal
Option_B: are required to back down
Option_C: may sound the danger signal
Option_D: should sound one short blast to show that you are holding course and speed
Correct_Answer: must sound the danger signal

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Your vessel is meeting another vessel head-on. To comply with the rules, you should exchange ______.
Option_A: one short blast, alter course to the left, and pass   starboard to starboard
Option_B: two short blasts, alter course to the left, and pass  starboard to starboard
Option_C: one short blast, alter course to the right, and pass port to port
Option_D: two short blasts, alter course to the right, and pass port to port
Correct_Answer: one short blast, alter course to the right, and pass port to port

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which indicates the presence of a partly  submerged object being towed?
Option_A: A diamond shape on the towed object
Option_B: An all-round light at each end of the towed object
Option_C: A searchlight beamed from the towing vessel in the direction of the tow
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY The light used to signal passing intentions is a(n) _____.
Option_A: all-round white light ONLY
Option_B: all-round yellow light ONLY
Option_C: all-round white or yellow light
Correct_Answer: all-round white or yellow light

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Two vessels in a crossing situation have reached agreement by radiotelephone as to the intentions of the  other. In this situation, whistle signals are __________.
Option_A: required
Option_B: not required, but may be sounded
Option_C: required if crossing within half a mile
Option_D: required when crossing within one mile
Correct_Answer: not required, but may be sounded

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are underway in a narrow channel, and are being overtaken by another power-driven vessel. The overtaking vessel sounds the signal indicating his intention to pass you on your starboard side. You signal your agreement by sounding _______________________.
Option_A: one short blast
Option_B: two prolonged blasts
Option_C: two prolonged followed by two short blasts
Option_D: one prolonged, one short, one prolonged, and one short blast in that order
Correct_Answer: one short blast

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are meeting another vessel head-on and sound one short blast as a passing signal. The other vessel answers with two short blasts. What should be your next action?
Option_A: Pass on the other vessel's starboard side.
Option_B: Sound the danger signal.
Option_C: Pass astern of the other vessel.
Correct_Answer: Sound the danger signal.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY What lights are required for a barge being  pushed ahead, not being part of a composite unit?
Option_A: Sidelights and a sternlight
Option_B: Sidelights and a special flashing light
Option_C: Sidelights, a towing light, and a sternlight
Option_D: Sidelights, a special flashing light, and a sternlight
Correct_Answer: Sidelights and a special flashing light

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are overtaking another power-driven vessel in a narrow channel, and you wish to overtake on the other vessel's port side. You will sound a whistle signal of  _______.
Option_A: one short blast
Option_B: two short blasts
Option_C: two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast
Option_D: two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts
Correct_Answer: two short blasts

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY At night, a barge moored in a slip used   primarily for mooring purposes shall ___________________.
Option_A: not be required to be lighted
Option_B: show a white light at each corner
Option_C: show a red light at the bow and stern
Option_D: show a flashing yellow light at each corner
Correct_Answer: not be required to be lighted

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A flashing blue light is used to identify  _____________________.
Option_A: law enforcement vessels
Option_B: U.S. submarines
Option_C: air-cushion vessels in the nondisplacement mode
Correct_Answer: law enforcement vessels

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which statement is TRUE concerning the fog  signal of a vessel 15 meters in length anchored in a  "special anchorage area" approved by the Secretary of  Transportation?
Option_A: The vessel is not required to sound a fog signal.
Option_B: The vessel shall ring a bell for 5 seconds every minute.
Option_C: The vessel shall sound one blast of the foghorn every 2  minutes.
Option_D: The vessel shall sound three blasts on the whistle every 2 minutes.
Correct_Answer: The vessel is not required to sound a fog signal.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A power-driven vessel, when leaving a dock or berth, is required to sound _____.
Option_A: four short blasts
Option_B: one long blast
Option_C: one prolonged blast
Correct_Answer: one prolonged blast

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which statement is TRUE concerning the Inland Navigation Rules?
Option_A: They list requirements for Traffic Separation Schemes.
Option_B: They define moderate speed.
Option_C: They require communication by radiotelephone to reach a  passing agreement.
Correct_Answer: They list requirements for Traffic Separation Schemes.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Whistle signals shall be exchanged by vessels in sight of one another when _____.
Option_A: they are passing within half a mile of each other
Option_B: passing agreements have been made by radio
Option_C: course changes are necessary to pass
Option_D: doubt exists as to which side the vessels will pass on
Correct_Answer: they are passing within half a mile of each other

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A barge more than 50 meters long would be  required to show how many white anchor lights when anchored in a Secretary of Transportation approved "special anchorage area"?
INLAND ONLY Your vessel must remain in a narrow channel for safe operation. Another vessel is crossing the channel  from your starboard. You do not think she will pass safely. You MUST ____________.
Option_A: stop your vessel, since the other vessel has the right of way
Option_B: sound one short blast of the whistle, and turn to starboard
Option_C: sound the danger signal
Option_D: stop your engines, and you may sound the danger signal
Correct_Answer: sound the danger signal

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY While underway during the day you sight a small motorboat showing a flashing blue light. The blue light indicates a __________________.
Option_A: law enforcement boat
Option_B: boat involved in a race
Option_C: Coast Guard Auxiliary Vessel on regatta patrol
Correct_Answer: law enforcement boat

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY While underway, you sight the lights illustrated in DIAGRAM 81, with the yellow lights flashing. You should _____________________.
Option_A: wait until the vessel ahead crosses your bow
Option_B: stop until the red lights turn green
Option_C: proceed leaving all the lights on your starboard side
Option_D: pass between the two sets of vertical red lights
Correct_Answer: pass between the two sets of vertical red lights

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY When power-driven vessels are in a crossing  situation, one short blast by either vessel would mean ____.
Option_A: "I intend to leave you on my port side"
Option_B: "I intend to hold course and speed"
Option_C: "I intend to change course to starboard"
Option_D: "I request a departure from the rules"
Correct_Answer: "I intend to leave you on my port side"

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Two vessels are meeting on a clear day and will pass less than half a mile apart. In this situation whistle signals ___________________.
Option_A: must be exchanged
Option_B: may be exchanged
Option_C: must be exchanged if passing agreements have not been made by radio
Option_D: must be exchanged only if course changes are necessary by either vessel
Correct_Answer: must be exchanged if passing agreements have not been made by radio

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Your power-driven vessel is overtaking another power-driven vessel in a narrow channel. You wish to overtake her on her starboard side. You should sound a whistle signal of _____.
Option_A: one short blast
Option_B: two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast
Option_C: one prolonged and one short blast
Correct_Answer: one short blast

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which is TRUE of a vessel downbound with a  following current when meeting an upbound vessel on the  Western Rivers?
Option_A: She has the right-of-way only if she is a power-driven  vessel.
Option_B: She has the right-of-way only if she has a tow.
Option_C: She does not have the right-of-way, since the other vessel is not crossing the river.
Option_D: She must wait for a whistle signal from the upbound vessel.
Correct_Answer: She has the right-of-way only if she is a power-driven  vessel.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A vessel of less than 20 meters in length at anchor at night in a "special anchorage area designated by the Secretary" _____.
Option_A: must show one white light
Option_B: need not show any lights
Option_C: must show two white lights
Option_D: need show a light only on the approach of another vessel
Correct_Answer: need not show any lights

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY At night, which lights are required on barges moored in group formation at a bank of a river?
Option_A: A white light placed at the corners farthest from the bank on each of the upstream and downstream ends of the group.
Option_B: A white light placed at the corners farthest from the bank of each barge in the group.
Option_C: A flashing yellow light placed at each of the upstream and downstream ends of the group.
Option_D: Two red lights in a vertical line placed at the corners  farthest from the bank on each of the upstream and   downstream ends of the group.
Correct_Answer: A white light placed at the corners farthest from the bank on each of the upstream and downstream ends of the group.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A power-driven vessel intends to overtake another power-driven vessel on the overtaken vessel's port side. Which whistle signal  should be sounded in order to state this intention?
Option_A: 1 short blast
Option_B: 2 short blasts
Option_C: 2 prolonged and 1 short blasts
Correct_Answer: 2 short blasts

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A towing vessel pushing ahead on the Western Rivers above the Huey P. Long bridge must show _________.
Option_A: sidelights only
Option_B: sidelights and towing lights
Option_C: sidelights, towing lights, and two masthead lights
Option_D: sidelights, towing lights, and three masthead lights
Correct_Answer: sidelights and towing lights

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A power-driven vessel, when leaving a dock or berth, is required to sound _____________________.
Option_A: two short blasts
Option_B: one long blast
Option_C: one prolonged blast
Correct_Answer: one prolonged blast

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which is CORRECT regarding a "special flashing light?"
Option_A: It must be yellow in color.
Option_B: It must be placed as far forward as possible.
Option_C: It must not show through an arc of more than 225°.
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY For the purpose of the Inland Navigation Rules, the term "Inland Waters" includes _________________.
Option_A: the Western Rivers, extending to the COLREGS demarcation line
Option_B: harbors and rivers to the outermost aids to navigation
Option_C: waters along the coast of the United States to a distance of two miles offshore
Correct_Answer: the Western Rivers, extending to the COLREGS demarcation line

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which is TRUE of a power-driven vessel, bound downstream, when meeting an upbound vessel on the Western Rivers?
Option_A: She has the right-of-way.
Option_B: She shall propose the manner of passage.
Option_C: She shall initiate maneuvering signals.
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are overtaking a power-driven vessel in a narrow channel and wish to leave her on your starboard side. You may  ________________________.
Option_A: sound one short blast
Option_B: sound four short blasts
Option_C: overtake her without sounding whistle signals
Option_D: attempt to contact her on the radiotelephone to arrange for the passage
Correct_Answer: attempt to contact her on the radiotelephone to arrange for the passage

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which term is NOT used in the Inland   Navigation Rules?
Option_A: A vessel engaged in mineclearing operations
Option_B: A vessel constrained by her draft
Option_C: A vessel towing
Correct_Answer: A vessel constrained by her draft

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A special flashing light is used on a vessel(s) ___________________.
Option_A: being pushed ahead
Option_B: at anchor in a fairway
Option_C: towed astern
Correct_Answer: being pushed ahead

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Under the Inland Navigation Rules, what is the meaning of a one short blast signal used when meeting  another vessel?
Option_A: "I am turning to starboard."
Option_B: "I am turning to port."
Option_C: "I intend to leave you on my starboard side."
Option_D: "I intend to leave you on my port side."
Correct_Answer: "I intend to leave you on my port side."

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY On the Western Rivers, a power-driven vessel crossing a river must _________________.
Option_A: maintain course and speed as you have the right of way over all vessels
Option_B: keep out of the way of any vessel descending the river
Option_C: keep out of the way of a power-driven vessel ascending or descending the river
Correct_Answer: keep out of the way of a power-driven vessel ascending or descending the river

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY While underway at night, you see two yellow  lights displayed in a vertical line. This should indicate to you a(n) _______________________.
Option_A: opening in a pipeline
Option_B: vessel broken down
Option_C: vessel pushing ahead
Correct_Answer: vessel pushing ahead

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY When two power-driven vessels are meeting on the Great Lakes, Western Rivers, or waters specified by the Secretary, where there is a current, which vessel shall §sound the first passing signal?
Option_A: The vessel going upstream stemming the current
Option_B: The vessel downbound with a following current
Option_C: The vessel that is towing regardless of the current
Correct_Answer: The vessel downbound with a following current

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A vessel leaving a dock or berth must sound a prolonged blast of the whistle only if ____________________.
Option_A: other vessels can be seen approaching
Option_B: she is a power-driven vessel
Option_C: visibility is restricted
Correct_Answer: she is a power-driven vessel

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY If your tug is pushing a barge ahead at night and it is not a composite unit, which light(s) should show aft on your vessel?
Option_A: A white sternlight
Option_B: Two red lights
Option_C: Two towing lights
Option_D: A towing light over the sternlight
Correct_Answer: Two towing lights

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are in charge of a power-driven vessel crossing a river on the Western Rivers. You must keep out of the way of a _____________.
Option_A: sail vessel descending the river
Option_B: power-driven vessel ascending the river
Option_C: sail vessel ascending the river
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A power-driven vessel crossing a river on the Great Lakes or Western Rivers, must keep out of the way of a power-driven vessel _________________________.
Option_A: descending the river with a tow
Option_B: ascending the river with a tow
Option_C: ascending the river without a tow
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY What is the whistle signal used to indicate a power-driven vessel leaving a dock?
Option_A: One short blast
Option_B: Three short blasts
Option_C: One prolonged blast
Correct_Answer: One prolonged blast

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which statement is TRUE concerning the light used for maneuvering signals?
Option_A: It must be synchronized with the whistle.
Option_B: It may be white or yellow.
Option_C: It must be an all-round light.
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Your vessel must stay within a narrow channel to be navigated safely. Another vessel is crossing your course from starboard to port. You do NOT think she will pass safely. You ______________________________.
Option_A: may sound the danger signal
Option_B: must sound the danger signal
Option_C: should sound one short blast to indicate that you are  holding course and speed
Correct_Answer: must sound the danger signal

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Two vessels are in a starboard to starboard  meeting situation and will pass well clear approximately§1/4 mile apart. Which action should each vessel take?
Option_A: Sound a one blast whistle signal and turn to starboard.
Option_B: Maintain course and sound no signal.
Option_C: Sound a two blast whistle signal and maintain course.
Option_D: Sound a three blast whistle signal and turn to port.
Correct_Answer: Sound a two blast whistle signal and maintain course.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A power-driven vessel pushing ahead or towing alongside on the Mississippi River, below the Huey P. Long Bridge, shall carry ______________.
Option_A: two masthead lights, sidelights and sternlight
Option_B: two masthead lights, sidelights and two towing lights
Option_C: sidelights and two towing lights
Option_D: one masthead light, sidelights and sternlight
Correct_Answer: two masthead lights, sidelights and two towing lights

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY While underway in a harbor you hear a vessel sound a prolonged blast. This signal indicates that this vessel _____________.
Option_A: desires to overtake your vessel
Option_B: is at anchor
Option_C: is backing her engines
Correct_Answer: is moving from a dock

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are overtaking another power-driven vessel and sound a whistle signal indicating that you intend to pass the vessel along her starboard side. If the other vessel answers your signal with five short and rapid blasts, you should _______.
Option_A: not overtake the other vessel until both vessels exchange the same passing signal
Option_B: not overtake the other vessel until she sounds another five short and rapid blast signal
Option_C: pass the other vessel along her starboard side
Option_D: sound five short and rapid blasts and pass along her  starboard side
Correct_Answer: not overtake the other vessel until both vessels exchange the same passing signal

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are meeting another vessel in inland waters, and she sounds one short blast on the whistle. This means that she _____.
Option_A: is changing course to starboard
Option_B: is changing course to port
Option_C: intends to leave you on her port side
Option_D: desires to depart from the Rules
Correct_Answer: intends to leave you on her port side

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are approaching a sharp bend in a river. You have sounded a prolonged blast and it has been answered by a vessel on the other side of the bend. Which statement is TRUE?

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which statement is TRUE concerning a passing agreement made by radiotelephone?
Option_A: Such an agreement is prohibited by the Rules.
Option_B: A vessel which has made such an agreement must also sound whistle signals.
Option_C: Whistle signals must still be exchanged when passing within half a mile of each other.

Correct_Answer: If agreement is reached by radiotelephone, whistle signals are optional.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are aboard the stand-on vessel in a crossing situation. You sound a one blast whistle signal. The  give-way vessel answers with a two blast whistle signal. You should sound the danger signal and _____.
Option_A: maintain course and speed as you are the stand-on vessel
Option_B: come around sharply to port
Option_C: take precautionary action until a safe passing agreement is made

Correct_Answer: take precautionary action until a safe passing agreement is made

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A power-driven vessel when pushing ahead or  towing alongside on the Western Rivers (above the Huey P. Long Bridge on the Mississippi River) shall exhibit   _______________________.
Option_A: two masthead lights, sidelights, and sternlight

Option_C: sidelights and two towing lights
Option_D: one masthead light, sidelights, and sternlight
Correct_Answer: sidelights and two towing lights

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Only law enforcement vessels are permitted to show ___________________.
Option_A: two red lights in a vertical line
Option_B: a flashing yellow light
Option_C: an alternately flashing red and yellow light
Correct_Answer: a flashing blue light

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are overtaking another power-driven vessel in a narrow channel. The other vessel will have to move to allow you to pass. You wish to overtake the other vessel on her   starboard side. Your first whistle signal should be  _______________________.
Option_A: one short blast
Option_B: two short blasts
Option_C: two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast
Option_D: two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts
Correct_Answer: one short blast

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which light display would mark the opening in a pipeline where vessels could pass through?
Option_A: Three red lights in a vertical line on each side of the  opening
Option_B: Two red lights in a vertical line on each side of the  opening
Option_C: Three white lights in a vertical line on each side of the opening
Option_D: Two white lights in a vertical line on each side of the  opening
Correct_Answer: Two red lights in a vertical line on each side of the  opening

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which light(s) shall be shown at night on a  moored barge which reduces the navigable width of any  channel to less than 80 meters?
Option_A: A white light placed on the two corners farthest from the bank
Option_B: Two yellow lights in a vertical line at the stern
Option_C: A red light placed on all four corners
Option_D: A red light placed on the two corners farthest from the bank
Correct_Answer: A white light placed on the two corners farthest from the bank

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are overtaking another power-driven vessel in a narrow channel. The other vessel will have to move to allow you to pass. You wish to overtake the other vessel and leave her on your starboard side. Your FIRST whistle signal should be ______________________.
Option_A: one short blast
Option_B: two short blasts
Option_C: two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast
Option_D: two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts
Correct_Answer: two short blasts

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are overtaking another power-driven vessel and sound a whistle signal indicating that you intend to pass the vessel along her starboard side. If the other vessel answers your signal with five short and rapid blasts, you should _______.
Option_A: pass the other vessel along her starboard side

Option_C: not overtake the other vessel until both vessels exchange the same passing signal
Option_D: not overtake the other vessel until she sounds another five short and rapid blast signal
Correct_Answer: not overtake the other vessel until both vessels exchange the same passing signal

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A power-driven vessel intends to overtake  another power-driven vessel on the overtaken vessel's port side. What whistle signal should be sounded in order to  state this intention?
Option_A: 1 prolonged and 1 short blast
Option_B: 1 short blast
Option_C: 2 prolonged and 2 short blasts
Correct_Answer: 2 short blasts

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are overtaking another power-driven vessel in a narrow channel. The other vessel will have to move to allow you to pass. You wish to overtake the other vessel and leave her on your starboard side. Your first whistle signal should be ___________________.
Option_A: two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast
Option_B: two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts
Option_C: one short blast
Correct_Answer: two short blasts

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which statement is TRUE concerning the fog  signal of a sailing vessel 25 meters in length anchored in a  "special anchorage area" approved by the Secretary of  Transportation?

Correct_Answer: The vessel shall ring a bell for 5 seconds every minute.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which light display marks the opening in a  pipeline where vessels could pass through?

Option_B: Three red lights in a vertical line on each side of the  opening

Option_D: Three white lights in a vertical line on each side of the opening
Correct_Answer: Two red lights in a vertical line on each side of the  opening

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY At night, a barge moored in a slip used   primarily for mooring purposes shall _____________________.

Correct_Answer: not be required to be lighted

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY At night, what lights are required on barges moored in a group formation at a river bank?

Correct_Answer: A white light placed at the corners farthest from the bank on each of the upstream and downstream ends of the group

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY What is true of a "special flashing light"?
Option_A: It may show through an arc of 180°.
Option_B: It flashes at the rate of 120 flashes per minute.
Option_C: It is optional below the Baton Rouge Highway Bridge.
Correct_Answer: It may show through an arc of 180°.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which is a characteristic of a "special§flashing light"?
Option_A: It is required for all vessels being pushed ahead as  part of a composite unit.
Option_B: It must show through an arc of not less than 180° nor more than 225°.
Option_C: It must be of the same character and construction as the masthead light.
Correct_Answer: It must show through an arc of not less than 180° nor more than 225°.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY What MAY be used to indicate the presence of a partly submerged object being towed?
Option_A: A black cone, apex upward
Option_B: Two all-round yellow lights at each end of the tow
Option_C: The beam of a search light from the towing vessel shown in the direction of the tow
Correct_Answer: The beam of a search light from the towing vessel shown in the direction of the tow

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY What shall be used to indicate the presence of a partly submerged object being towed?
Option_A: A black cone, apex downward
Option_B: An all-round white light at each end of the tow
Option_C: A flare-up light
Correct_Answer: An all-round white light at each end of the tow

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A barge more than 50 meters long is required to show how many white anchor lights when anchored in a  Secretary of Transportation approved "special anchorage  area?"

Option_C: Two

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY What is not contained in the Inland Navigation Rules?

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Under the Inland Navigation Rules, the term  "Inland Waters" includes ________________.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are on board the stand-on vessel in a  crossing situation. You sound a one blast whistle signal, and the give-way vessel answers with a two-blast signal. You should then sound the danger signal and _______________.

Correct_Answer: stop and back your vessel if necessary until signals are agreed upon

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are proceeding in a channel in inland waters and are meeting an outbound vessel. Your responsibilities include _____.
Option_A: keeping to that side of the channel which is on your  vessel's port side
Option_B: exchanging whistle signals if passing within half a mile

Correct_Answer: exchanging whistle signals if passing within half a mile

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Your vessel must stay within a narrow channel to be navigated safely. Another vessel is crossing your course from starboard to port. You do NOT think she will pass  safely. You are required to ____________________.

Option_B: back down
Option_C: sound one short blast to indicate that you are holding course and speed
Correct_Answer: sound the danger signal

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are navigating in a narrow channel and must remain in the channel for safe operation. Another vessel is crossing the channel ahead of you from your starboard. You are doubtful of intention of the crossing vessel. You MUST __________________.
Option_A: stop your vessel, since the other vessel has the right  of way
Option_B: sound the danger signal
Option_C: contact him on the radiotelephone to make a passing   agreement
Option_D: stop your engines until you have slowed to bare steerageway
Correct_Answer: sound the danger signal

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which statement is TRUE of a power-driven vessel proceeding downbound with the current, when meeting an  upbound vessel on the Western Rivers?
Option_A: She shall not impede the upbound vessel.
Option_B: She shall pass on the port side of the other.
Option_C: She shall propose the manner of passage.
Correct_Answer: She shall propose the manner of passage.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A power-driven vessel operating in a narrow  channel with a following current on the Great Lakes or  Western Rivers is meeting an upbound vessel. Which   statement is TRUE?
Option_A: The downbound vessel has the right of way.
Option_B: The upbound vessel must initiate the required maneuvering signals.
Option_C: The upbound vessel must propose the manner of passing.
Correct_Answer: The downbound vessel has the right of way.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Which is TRUE of a vessel downbound with a  following current when meeting an upbound vessel on the  Western Rivers?
Option_A: Neither vessel has the right-of-way.
Option_B: She has the right-of-way only if she is power-driven.
Option_C: She does not have the right-of-way, since the other vessel is not crossing the river.
Option_D: She must wait for a whistle signal from the upbound vessel.
Correct_Answer: She has the right-of-way only if she is power-driven.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Yellow lights are NOT used to identify _______.
Option_A: a dredge pipeline on a trestle
Option_B: the heads of tows being pushed ahead by tugboats
Option_C: purse seiners
Correct_Answer: a seaplane on the water

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A vessel displaying an alternating red and  yellow light is __________.

Option_B: enforcing the law
Option_C: engaged in public safety activities
Option_D: restricted in its ability to maneuver

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A law enforcement vessel patrolling a marine regatta may show either a flashing blue light or ________.

Correct_Answer: an alternately flashing red and yellow light

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are the stand-on vessel in a crossing  situation. The other vessel is showing an alternating  red and yellow light. Which action should you take?

Option_B: Heave to.
Option_C: Alter course to assist.
Correct_Answer: Stand on.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY You are the stand-on vessel in an overtaking situation. The other vessel is showing an alternately  flashing red-and-yellow light. What action should you take?

Option_B: Give-way
Option_C: Stand on
Correct_Answer: Stand on

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY The special light for a vessel engaged in public safety activities must _____.

Correct_Answer: not interfere with the visibility of the navigation lights

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A light used to signal passing intentions must be an __________.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A light used to signal passing intentions must be an _______________________.
Option_A: all-round yellow light only

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A light used to signal passing intentions must be a(n) _____________________.
Option_A: all-round white or yellow light
Option_B: all-round yellow light only
Option_C: all-round white light only
Correct_Answer: all-round white or yellow light

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY What characteristic must a light have if used to signal passing intentions?
Option_A: It must be an all-round white light.
Option_B: It must be an alternating blue and white light.
Option_C: It must be either an all-round white or an all-round yellow light.
Option_D: It must be an alternating red and yellow light.
Correct_Answer: It must be either an all-round white or an all-round yellow light.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY What characteristic must a light used to  indicate passing intentions have?
Option_A: It must be an alternating red and yellow light.
Option_B: It must be an all-round white light.
Option_C: It must be an all-round yellow light.
Option_D: It must be either an all-round white or an all-round yellow light.
Correct_Answer: It must be either an all-round white or an all-round yellow light.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY In a narrow channel, you are underway on vessel "A" and desire to overtake vessel "B". After you sound two short blasts on your whistle, vessel "B" sounds five short and rapid blasts on the whistle. You should _______.
Option_A: pass with caution on the port side of vessel "B"

Correct_Answer: initiate another signal after the situation has stabilized

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY A power-driven vessel pushing ahead or towing alongside on the Mississippi River, above the Huey P. Long Bridge, shall carry _________.

Correct_Answer: A vessel trawling

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY You are on a vessel that cannot comply with the spacing requirement for masthead lights. What is required in this situation?

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY A single vessel being towed alongside shall show ______________________.

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY Signals shall be sounded by a power-driven  vessel intending to overtake _____.

Option_A: river bank protection
Option_B: conducting submarine operations
Option_C: firefighting
Correct_Answer: firefighting

Question_Text: INLAND ONLY One and two short blast signals must be§sounded on inland waters when ______.
Option_A: two sailing vessels are in sight of one another and meeting at a distance of one quarter mile
Option_B: two power-driven vessels are in sight of one another and will cross at a distance of one mile
Option_C: two power-driven vessels are crossing within half a mile of each other and NOT in sight of each other
Option_D: Two power-driven vessel are in sight of one another and are meeting at a distance of one half mile
Correct_Answer: Two power-driven vessel are in sight of one another and are meeting at a distance of one half mile

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You hear the fog signal of  another vessel forward of your beam. Risk of collision may exist. You MUST _____.
Option_A: begin a radar plot
Option_B: stop your engines
Option_C: take all way off, if necessary
Correct_Answer: take all way off, if necessary

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The rules require that a  §stand-on vessel SHALL take action to avoid collision when§she determines that _____.
Option_A: risk of collision exists
Option_B: the other vessel will cross ahead of her
Option_C: the other vessel is not taking appropriate action
Option_D: collision cannot be avoided by the give-way vessel's  maneuver alone
Correct_Answer: collision cannot be avoided by the give-way vessel's  maneuver alone

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your vessel is 75 meters in  length and restricted in her ability to maneuver.   Visibility is restricted. What signal do you sound if you are carrying out your work at anchor?
Option_A: Five seconds ringing of a bell at intervals of not more than one minute
Option_B: One prolonged blast followed by two short blasts on the  whistle at intervals of not more than two minutes
Option_C: Five seconds ringing of a bell and five second sounding of a gong at intervals of not more than one minute
Option_D: Four short blasts on the whistle at intervals of not more than two minutes
Correct_Answer: One prolonged blast followed by two short blasts on the  whistle at intervals of not more than two minutes

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway in fog, you hear a prolonged blast from another vessel. This signal   indicates a _________________.
Option_A: sailboat underway
Option_B: vessel underway, towing
Option_C: power-driven vessel underway, making way
Correct_Answer: power-driven vessel underway, making way

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is used to show the  presence of a partly submerged object being towed?
Option_A: A diamond shape on the towed object
Option_B: An all-round light at each end of the towed object
Option_C: A searchlight from the towing vessel in the direction of the tow
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND At night, a barge being towed astern must display ___________________.
Option_A: red and green sidelights only
Option_B: a white sternlight only
Option_C: sidelights and a sternlight
Correct_Answer: sidelights and a sternlight

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which signal is recognized as§a distress signal?
Option_A: Directing the beam of a searchlight at another vessel
Option_B: A smoke signal giving off orange colored smoke
Option_C: A whistle signal of one prolonged and three short blasts
Option_D: International Code Signal "PAN" spoken over theradiotelephone
Correct_Answer: A smoke signal giving off orange colored smoke

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your vessel is approaching a bend. You hear a prolonged blast from around the bend. You should _________________.
Option_A: back your engines
Option_B: stop your engines and drift
Option_C: answer with one prolonged blast
Correct_Answer: answer with one prolonged blast

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If you do NOT understand the course or intention of an approaching vessel you should  sound __________________.
Option_A: one short blast
Option_B: one prolonged blast
Option_C: not less than five short blasts
Option_D: not less than five prolonged blasts
Correct_Answer: not less than five short blasts

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If you are the stand-on vessel in a crossing situation, you may take action to avoid  collision by your maneuver alone. When may this action be taken?
Option_A: At any time you feel it is appropriate
Option_B: Only when you have reached extremis
Option_C: When you determine that your present course will cross ahead of the other vessel
Option_D: When it becomes apparent to you that the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action
Correct_Answer: When it becomes apparent to you that the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your 15-meter tug is underway and crossing a deep and narrow channel. A large container vessel is off your port bow on a steady bearing. Which  statement is TRUE concerning this situation?
Option_A: You should maintain course and speed.
Option_B: The container vessel is the stand-on as it is the  larger vessel.
Option_C: You are not to impede the safe passage of the container  vessel in the channel.
Correct_Answer: You are not to impede the safe passage of the container  vessel in the channel.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If your vessel is underway in fog and you hear one prolonged and three short blasts, this is a _____________________.
Option_A: vessel not under command
Option_B: sailing vessel
Option_C: vessel being towed (manned)
Correct_Answer: vessel being towed (manned)

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A pilot vessel on pilotage duty at night will show sidelights and a sternlight ___________.
Option_A: when at anchor
Option_B: only when making way
Option_C: at any time when underway
Option_D: only when the identifying lights are not being shown
Correct_Answer: at any time when underway

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel underway in fog making NO way must sound what signal?
Option_A: One long blast
Option_B: Two prolonged blasts
Option_C: One prolonged blast
Option_D: One prolonged and two short blasts
Correct_Answer: Two prolonged blasts

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 95-meter vessel aground  sounds which fog signal?
Option_A: A rapid ringing of a bell for 5 seconds every two minutes
Option_B: A whistle signal of one short, one prolonged, and one short blast
Option_C: A prolonged blast of the whistle at intervals not to exceed one minute
Option_D: A rapid ringing of a bell for 5 seconds, preceded and  followed by three separate and distinct strokes on the bell
Correct_Answer: A rapid ringing of a bell for 5 seconds, preceded and  followed by three separate and distinct strokes on the bell

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning a vessel equipped with operational radar?
Option_A: She must use this equipment to obtain early warning of risk of collision.
Option_B: The radar equipment is only required to be used in   restricted visibility.
Option_C: The use of a radar excuses a vessel from the need of a  look-out.
Option_D: The safe speed of such a vessel will likely be greater than that of vessels without radar.
Correct_Answer: She must use this equipment to obtain early warning of risk of collision.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 200-meter vessel is aground in fog. Which signal is optional?
Option_A: A bell signal
Option_B: A gong signal
Option_C: A whistle signal
Correct_Answer: A whistle signal

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which is a distress signal?
Option_A: A triangular flag above or below a ball
Option_B: The International Code Signal of distress indicated by "JV"
Option_C: A green smoke signal
Option_D: Flames on the vessel as from a burning tar barrel
Correct_Answer: Flames on the vessel as from a burning tar barrel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel must proceed at a safe speed _____.
Option_A: in restricted visibility
Option_B: in congested waters
Option_C: during darkness
Correct_Answer: at all times

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A light signal of three flashes means _________________.
Option_A: "I am in doubt as to your actions"
Option_B: "My engines are full speed astern"
Option_C: "I desire to overtake you"
Correct_Answer: "I am operating astern propulsion"

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A sailing vessel underway may exhibit ___________________.
Option_A: a red light over a green light at the masthead
Option_B: a green light over a red light at the masthead
Option_C: two white lights in a vertical line at the stern
Option_D: an all-round white light at the bow
Correct_Answer: a red light over a green light at the masthead

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A sailing vessel is overtaking a tug and tow as shown. Which statement is CORRECT?
Option_A: The sailing vessel is the stand-on vessel because it is  overtaking.
Option_B: The sailing vessel is the stand-on vessel because it is  under sail.
Option_C: The tug is the stand-on vessel because it is being   overtaken.
Option_D: The tug is the stand-on vessel because it is towing.
Correct_Answer: The tug is the stand-on vessel because it is being   overtaken.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The word "vessel", in the Rules, includes _____.
Option_A: sailing ships
Option_B: nondisplacement craft
Option_C: seaplanes
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A sailing vessel with the wind abaft the beam is navigating in fog. She should sound  ____________________.
Option_A: three short blasts
Option_B: one prolonged blast
Option_C: one prolonged and two short blasts
Correct_Answer: one prolonged and two short blasts

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which is a distress signal?
Option_A: Firing of green star shells
Option_B: Sounding 5 short blasts on the whistle
Option_C: Answering a one blast whistle signal with two blasts
Option_D: A flaming barrel of oil on deck
Correct_Answer: A flaming barrel of oil on deck

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If a towing vessel and her tow are severely restricted in their ability to change course, they may show lights in addition to their towing   identification lights. These additional lights may be shown if the tow is ________________.
Option_A: pushed ahead
Option_B: towed alongside
Option_C: towed astern
Correct_Answer: Any of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If two sailing vessels are  running free with the wind on the same side, which one must keep clear of the other?
Option_A: The one with the wind closest abeam
Option_B: The one with the wind closest astern
Option_C: The one to leeward
Correct_Answer: The one to windward

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY The masthead light may be  located at other than the fore and aft centerline on a power-driven vessel _________________.
Option_A: less than 20 meters in length
Option_B: less than 12 meters in length
Option_C: which has separate sidelights carried on the outboard  extremes of the vessel's breadth
Correct_Answer: less than 12 meters in length

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The NAVIGATION RULES define a "vessel not under command" as a vessel which ______________.
Option_A: from the nature of her work is unable to keep out of the way of another vessel
Option_B: through some exceptional circumstance is unable to maneuver as required by the rules
Option_C: by taking action contrary to the rules has created a special circumstance situation
Option_D: is moored, aground or anchored in a fairway
Correct_Answer: through some exceptional circumstance is unable to maneuver as required by the rules

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Additional light signals are provided in the Annexes to the Rules for vessels __________.
Option_A: engaged in fishing
Option_B: not under command
Option_C: engaged in towing
Correct_Answer: engaged in fishing

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel may combine her sidelights and sternlight in one lantern on the fore and aft centerline of the vessel?
Option_A: A 16-meter sailing vessel
Option_B: A 25-meter power-driven vessel
Option_C: A 28-meter sailing vessel
Correct_Answer: A 16-meter sailing vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The duration of a prolonged  blast of the whistle is __________________.
Option_A: 2 to 4 seconds
Option_B: 4 to 6 seconds
Option_C: 6 to 8 seconds
Correct_Answer: 4 to 6 seconds

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel "restricted in her  ability to maneuver" is one which _____.
Option_A: from the nature of her work is unable to maneuver as  required by the rules
Option_B: through some exceptional circumstance is unable to maneuver as required by the rules
Option_C: due to adverse weather conditions is unable to maneuver as required by the rules
Option_D: has lost steering and is unable to maneuver
Correct_Answer: from the nature of her work is unable to maneuver as  required by the rules

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When underway in restricted  visibility, you might hear, at intervals of two minutes, any of the following fog signals EXCEPT _________________.
Option_A: one prolonged blast
Option_B: two prolonged blasts
Option_C: one prolonged and two short blasts
Option_D: ringing of a bell for five seconds
Correct_Answer: ringing of a bell for five seconds

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are preparing to cross a§narrow channel. You see a vessel that can only be navigated§safely within the channel. You should ___________.
Option_A: not cross the channel if you might impede the other vessel
Option_B: initiate an exchange of passing signals
Option_C: sound the danger signal
Correct_Answer: not cross the channel if you might impede the other vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A bell is used to sound a fog signal for a _________________.
Option_A: power-driven vessel underway
Option_B: sailing vessel at anchor
Option_C: vessel engaged in fishing
Correct_Answer: sailing vessel at anchor

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You see another vessel   approaching, and its compass bearing does not significantly change. This would indicate that _____.
Option_A: you are the stand-on vessel
Option_B: risk of collision exists
Option_C: a special circumstances situation exists
Option_D: the other vessel is dead in the water
Correct_Answer: risk of collision exists

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A towing vessel pushing a barge ahead and rigidly connected in a composite unit shall show the lights of _________________.
Option_A: a vessel towing by pushing ahead
Option_B: a power-driven vessel, not towing
Option_C: a barge being pushed ahead
Option_D: either answer A or answer B
Correct_Answer: a power-driven vessel, not towing

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are the watch officer on a power-driven vessel and notice a large sailing vessel  approaching from astern. You should _____.
Option_A: slow down
Option_B: sound one short blast and change course to starboard
Option_C: sound two short blasts and change course to port
Correct_Answer: hold your course and speed

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel shall be deemed to§be overtaking when she can see at night ________.
Option_A: only the sternlight of the vessel
Option_B: a sidelight and one masthead light of the vessel
Option_C: only a sidelight of the vessel
Option_D: any lights except the masthead lights of the vessel
Correct_Answer: only the sternlight of the vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel trawling will display a ____________________.
Option_A: red light over a white light
Option_B: green light over a white light
Option_C: yellow light over a red light
Option_D: white light over a green light
Correct_Answer: green light over a white light

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If it becomes necessary for a stand-on vessel to take action to avoid collision, she  shall NOT, if possible, _____.
Option_A: decrease speed
Option_B: increase speed
Option_C: turn to port for a vessel on her own port side
Option_D: turn to starboard for a vessel on her own port side
Correct_Answer: turn to port for a vessel on her own port side

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your vessel is NOT making way, but is not in any way disabled. Another vessel is approaching you on your starboard beam. Which statement is TRUE?
Option_A: The other vessel must give way since your vessel is stopped.
Option_B: Your vessel is the give-way vessel in a crossing situation.
Option_C: You should be showing the lights or shapes for a vessel not under command.
Option_D: You should be showing the lights or shapes for a vessel  restricted in her ability to maneuver.
Correct_Answer: Your vessel is the give-way vessel in a crossing situation.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 22-meter sailing vessel when also being propelled by machinery shall show during daylight hours a _______________________.
Option_A: black diamond
Option_B: black cone
Option_C: black ball
Correct_Answer: black cone

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The rules concerning lights  shall be complied with in all weathers from sunset to  sunrise. The lights _____.
Option_A: shall be displayed in restricted visibility during daylight hours
Option_B: need not be displayed when no other vessels are in the area
Option_C: shall be set at low power when used during daylight hours
Option_D: need not be displayed by unmanned vessels
Correct_Answer: shall be displayed in restricted visibility during daylight hours

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Two vessels meeting in a "head- on" situation are directed by the Rules to ________________.
Option_A: alter course to starboard and pass port to port
Option_B: alter course to port and pass starboard to starboard
Option_C: decide on which side the passage will occur by matching  whistle signals
Correct_Answer: alter course to starboard and pass port to port

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel is "engaged in fishing" when ___________________.
Option_A: her gear extends more than 100 meters from the vessel
Option_B: she is using any type of gear, other than lines
Option_C: she is using fishing apparatus which restricts her   maneuverability
Option_D: she has any fishing gear on board
Correct_Answer: she is using fishing apparatus which restricts her   maneuverability

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When shall the stand-on vessel change course and speed?
Option_A: The stand-on vessel may change course and speed at any time as it has the right-of-way
Option_B: After the give-way vessel sounds one blast in a crossing situation
Option_C: When action by the give-way vessel alone cannot prevent  collision
Option_D: When the two vessels become less than half a mile apart
Correct_Answer: When action by the give-way vessel alone cannot prevent  collision

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A sailing vessel with the wind abaft the beam is navigating in restricted visibility. She should sound _________________.
Option_A: three short blasts
Option_B: one prolonged blast
Option_C: one prolonged and two short blasts
Correct_Answer: one prolonged and two short blasts

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You see a vessel displaying the code flag "LIMA" below which is a red ball. The vessel is§_____.
Option_A: trolling
Option_B: getting ready to receive aircraft
Option_C: aground
Correct_Answer: in distress

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which factor is listed in the Rules as one which must be taken into account when   determining safe speed?
Option_A: The construction of the vessel
Option_B: The maneuverability of the vessel
Option_C: The experience of vessel personnel
Option_D: All of the above must be taken into account.
Correct_Answer: The maneuverability of the vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning seaplanes on the water?
Option_A: A seaplane must show appropriate lights but need not exhibit shapes.
Option_B: A seaplane should exhibit the lights for a vessel   constrained by her draft.
Option_C: In situations where a risk of collision exists, a seaplane should always give way.
Option_D: A seaplane on the water shall, in general, keep well clear of all vessels.
Correct_Answer: A seaplane on the water shall, in general, keep well clear of all vessels.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are in charge of a§power-driven vessel navigating at night. You sight the red§sidelight of another vessel on your port bow. The other§vessel's after masthead light is to the right of her forward§masthead light. You should _____.
Option_A: hold course and speed
Option_B: alter course to port
Option_C: stop engines
Correct_Answer: hold course and speed

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND There are two classes of vessels which, to the extent necessary to carry out their work, do not have to comply with the rule regarding traffic   separation schemes. One of these is a vessel _____________.
Option_A: engaged in fishing in a traffic lane
Option_B: servicing a submarine cable
Option_C: towing another
Correct_Answer: servicing a submarine cable

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway in fog when you hear the rapid ringing of a bell for five seconds followed by the sounding of a gong for five seconds. This signal indicates a vessel ___________________.
Option_A: aground
Option_B: more than 100 meters in length, at anchor
Option_C: fishing while making no way through the water
Option_D: fishing in company with another vessel
Correct_Answer: more than 100 meters in length, at anchor

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND At night, which lights are  required to be shown by a dredge on the side of the dredge which another vessel may pass?
Option_A: One red light
Option_B: Two red lights
Option_C: One white light
Correct_Answer: Two green lights

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which lights are shown by a  vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver to indicate that the vessel is making way?
Option_A: Masthead lights, sidelights and sternlight
Option_B: Masthead lights and sidelights only
Option_C: Sidelights and sternlight only
Correct_Answer: Masthead lights, sidelights and sternlight

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway and hear a  vessel continuously sounding her fog whistle. This   indicates the other vessel _________________.
Option_A: desires to communicate by radio
Option_B: desires a pilot
Option_C: is in distress
Correct_Answer: is in distress

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 30-meter tug is underway and NOT towing. At night, this vessel must show sidelights and _____.
Option_A: one masthead light and a sternlight
Option_B: two masthead lights and a sternlight
Option_C: three masthead lights and a sternlight
Correct_Answer: one masthead light and a sternlight

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway in fog, you hear a signal of one prolonged blast followed by three short  blasts. This is the fog signal for a vessel ___________.
Option_A: towing
Option_B: manned being towed
Option_C: unmanned being towed
Correct_Answer: manned being towed

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning a vessel of 75 meters in length, at anchor?
Option_A: She must show an all-round white light forward.
Option_B: She must show a second all-round white light aft.
Option_C: She may use her working lights to illuminate her decks.
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are approaching another  vessel. She is about one mile distant and is on your  starboard bow. You believe she will cross ahead of   you. She then sounds a whistle signal of five    short blasts. You should _______________________.
Option_A: answer the signal and hold course and speed
Option_B: reduce speed slightly to make sure she will have room to pass
Option_C: make a large course change, and slow down if necessary
Option_D: wait for another whistle signal from the other vessel
Correct_Answer: make a large course change, and slow down if necessary

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If a rowboat underway does NOT show the lights specified for a sailing vessel underway, it shall show a _________________.
Option_A: white light from sunset to sunrise
Option_B: combined lantern showing green to starboard and red to port and shown from sunset to sunrise
Option_C: combined lantern showing green to starboard and red to port and shown in sufficient time to prevent collision
Option_D: white light shown in sufficient time to prevent collision
Correct_Answer: white light shown in sufficient time to prevent collision

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel at anchor shall  display, between sunrise and sunset, on the forward part of the vessel where it can best be seen ___________________.
Option_A: one black ball
Option_B: two black balls
Option_C: one red ball
Correct_Answer: one black ball

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway in fog and hear a fog signal of two prolonged blasts on your starboard  quarter. You should _____.
Option_A: stop your vessel
Option_B: change course to the left
Option_C: change course to the right
Correct_Answer: hold your course and speed

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway, in fog, when you hear a whistle signal of one prolonged blast followed by two short blasts. This signal could indicate a vessel  ___________________.
Option_A: not under command
Option_B: being towed
Option_C: aground
Correct_Answer: not under command

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel must exhibit three white masthead lights in a vertical line?
Option_A: Any vessel towing astern
Option_B: A vessel whose tow exceeds 200 meters astern
Option_C: A vessel not under command, at anchor
Correct_Answer: A vessel whose tow exceeds 200 meters astern

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND All of the following are  distress signals EXCEPT _________________.
Option_A: the continuous sounding of any fog signal apparatus
Option_B: giving five or more short and rapid blasts of the whistle
Option_C: firing a gun at intervals of about a minute
Option_D: a barrel with burning oil in it, on deck
Correct_Answer: giving five or more short and rapid blasts of the whistle

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If you are approaching a bend, and hear a whistle signal of one prolonged blast from around the bend, you should answer with a signal of _____________.
Option_A: a short blast
Option_B: a prolonged blast
Option_C: one short, one prolonged, and one short blast
Correct_Answer: a prolonged blast

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel must show an after masthead light, if over 50 meters in length?
Option_A: A vessel engaged in fishing
Option_B: A vessel at anchor
Option_C: A vessel not under command
Correct_Answer: A vessel trawling

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A "flashing light", by the  definition given in the rules, is a light that _______.
Option_A: is red in color
Option_B: is visible over an arc of the horizon of 360°
Option_C: flashes at regular intervals at a frequency of 120 flashes or more per minute
Correct_Answer: flashes at regular intervals at a frequency of 120 flashes or more per minute

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The term "restricted visibility" as used in the Rules refers ___________________.
Option_A: only to fog
Option_B: only to visibility of less than one-half of a mile
Option_C: to visibility where you cannot see shore
Option_D: to any condition where visibility is restricted
Correct_Answer: to any condition where visibility is restricted

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL AND INLAND A vessel engaged in   mineclearing shows special identity lights _____.
Option_A: in addition to the lights required for a power-driven vessel
Option_B: which mean that other vessels should not approach within 1000 meters of the mineclearing vessel
Option_C: which are green and show all-round
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND According to the Navigation  Rules, you may depart from the Rules when _______________.
Option_A: no vessels are in sight visually
Option_B: no vessels are visible on radar
Option_C: you are in immediate danger
Correct_Answer: you are in immediate danger

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND An authorized light to assist in the identification of submarines operating on the surface is a(n) ________________.
Option_A: blue rotating light
Option_B: intermittent flashing amber/yellow light
Option_C: flashing white light
Correct_Answer: intermittent flashing amber/yellow light

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning two sailing vessels?
Option_A: A sailing vessel with the wind forward of the beam on her port side shall keep out of the way of a sailing vessel with the wind forward of the beam on the starboard side.
Option_B: When both vessels have the wind on the same side, the vessel to leeward shall keep out of the way.
Option_C: A sail vessel with the wind abaft of the beam must keep out of the way of a vessel sailing into the wind.
Correct_Answer: A sailing vessel with the wind forward of the beam on her port side shall keep out of the way of a sailing vessel with the wind forward of the beam on the starboard side.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When underway in a channel, you should keep to the _____.
Option_A: middle of the channel
Option_B: starboard side of the channel
Option_C: port side of the channel
Option_D: side of the channel that has the widest turns
Correct_Answer: starboard side of the channel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway, in fog, you hear a whistle signal of one prolonged blast followed by two  short blasts. This signal is sounded by a vessel   ___________.
Option_A: not under command
Option_B: being towed
Option_C: on pilotage duty
Correct_Answer: not under command

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When navigating in restricted visibility, a power-driven vessel shall ________________.
Option_A: stop her engines when hearing a fog signal forward of her beam, even if risk of collision does not exist
Option_B: have her engines ready for immediate maneuver
Option_C: when making way, sound one prolonged blast at intervals of not more than one minute
Option_D: operate at a speed to be able to stop in the distance of her visibility
Correct_Answer: have her engines ready for immediate maneuver

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You can indicate that your  vessel is in distress by ___________________.
Option_A: displaying a large red flag
Option_B: displaying three black balls in a vertical line
Option_C: sounding four or more short rapid blasts on the whistle
Correct_Answer: continuously sounding the fog whistle

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND During the day, a dredge will indicate the side on which it is safe to pass by displaying _________________.
Option_A: two balls in a vertical line
Option_B: two diamonds in a vertical line
Option_C: a single black ball
Option_D: no shape is shown during the day
Correct_Answer: two diamonds in a vertical line

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 45-meter vessel is pulling a 210-meter tow. She may exhibit ________________.
Option_A: a masthead light forward, and two masthead lights in a  vertical line aft
Option_B: three masthead lights forward and one aft
Option_C: two masthead lights forward and no after masthead light
Option_D: three masthead lights aft and none forward
Correct_Answer: three masthead lights forward and one aft

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is§TRUE concerning the danger signal?
Option_A: When any vessel fails to understand the intentions of an approaching vessel she must sound the danger signal.
Option_B: Only the stand-on vessel can sound the danger signal.
Option_C: Distress signals may be used in place of the danger signal.
Option_D: The danger signal consists of 4 or more short blasts of the whistle.
Correct_Answer: When any vessel fails to understand the intentions of an approaching vessel she must sound the danger signal.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A distress signal _____________.
Option_A: consists of 5 or more short blasts of the fog signal  apparatus
Option_B: may be used separately or with other distress signals
Option_C: consists of the raising and lowering of a large white flag
Option_D: is used to indicate doubt about another vessel's intentions
Correct_Answer: may be used separately or with other distress signals

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which is the danger signal?
Option_A: A continuous sounding of the fog signal
Option_B: Firing a gun every minute
Option_C: Five or more short rapid blasts on the whistle
Option_D: One prolonged blast on the whistle
Correct_Answer: Five or more short rapid blasts on the whistle

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel is "in sight" of  another vessel when ___________________.
Option_A: she can be observed by radar
Option_B: she can be observed visually from the other vessel
