Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are crossing a narrow  channel in an 18-meter tug when you sight a loaded tankship off your port bow coming up the channel. Which statement is correct?
Option_A: Neither vessel is the stand-on vessel because the tankship is crossing.
Option_B: You cannot impede the safe passage of the tankship.
Option_C: The tankship is the stand-on vessel because it is in the  channel.
Option_D: The tankship is the stand-on vessel because it is the larger of the two vessels.
Correct_Answer: You cannot impede the safe passage of the tankship.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel engaged in fishing  underway sounds the same fog signal as a _________________.
Option_A: power-driven vessel stopped and making no way through the water
Option_B: vessel being towed
Option_C: vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver at anchor
Correct_Answer: vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver at anchor

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel 15 meters in length which is proceeding under sail as well as being propelled by machinery shall exhibit during the daytime _______________.
Option_A: one black ball
Option_B: a basket
Option_C: a cone with its apex downward
Option_D: two cones with their apexes together
Correct_Answer: a cone with its apex downward

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel should not impede§the navigation of a power-driven vessel?
Option_A: A vessel not under command
Option_B: A vessel engaged in fishing
Option_C: A sailing vessel
Correct_Answer: A seaplane

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your vessel is underway but  stopped and making no way through the water when fog sets in. Which fog signal should you sound?
Option_A: One prolonged blast on the whistle
Option_B: One prolonged blast and two short blasts on the whistle
Option_C: Two prolonged blasts on the whistle
Option_D: One short, one prolonged, and one short blast on the whistle
Correct_Answer: Two prolonged blasts on the whistle

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel underway and fishing shall keep out of the way of a _____.
Option_A: power-driven vessel underway
Option_B: vessel not under command
Option_C: vessel sailing
Correct_Answer: vessel not under command

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The whistle signal for a vessel operating astern propulsion is _________________.
Option_A: one long blast
Option_B: one prolonged blast
Option_C: three short blasts
Correct_Answer: three short blasts

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND An anchored vessel is servicing an aid to navigation and is restricted in her ability to maneuver. Which lights will she show?
Option_A: Three all-round red-white-red lights in a vertical line and anchor lights
Option_B: Three all-round red-white-red lights in a vertical line ONLY
Option_C: Anchor lights ONLY
Correct_Answer: Three all-round red-white-red lights in a vertical line and anchor lights

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel is a "vessel  restricted in her ability to maneuver" under the Rules?
Option_A: A vessel mineclearing
Option_B: A vessel engaged in fishing
Option_C: A vessel at anchor
Correct_Answer: A vessel mineclearing

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What would NOT be a distress signal?
Option_A: "MAYDAY" sent by radiotelephone
Option_B: Continuous sounding of fog horn
Option_C: Green star shells fired from a launcher
Option_D: Square flag and ball in a vertical line
Correct_Answer: Green star shells fired from a launcher

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In a dense fog you hear a  whistle signal ahead of one prolonged blast followed by  three short blasts. This signal indicates a _____________.
Option_A: fishing vessel underway trawling
Option_B: manned vessel being towed
Option_C: pilot vessel underway making a special signal
Correct_Answer: manned vessel being towed

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A head-on situation at night is one in which you see _________________.
Option_A: one sidelight of a vessel ahead of you
Option_B: one sidelight and a masthead light of a vessel ahead of you
Option_C: one sidelight, a masthead light, and a range light of a  vessel ahead of you
Option_D: both sidelights of a vessel dead ahead of you
Correct_Answer: both sidelights of a vessel dead ahead of you

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are the stand-on vessel in a crossing situation. If you think the give-way vessel is NOT taking sufficient action to avoid collision, you should sound __________________.
Option_A: one short blast and maintain course
Option_B: two short blasts, alter to port, and pass astern
Option_C: no signal and maneuver at will
Correct_Answer: the danger signal

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A lantern combining the§two sidelights and sternlight may be shown on a __________.
Option_A: 10-meter sailing vessel
Option_B: 20-meter vessel engaged in fishing and making way
Option_C: 25-meter power-driven vessel engaged in trolling
Correct_Answer: 10-meter sailing vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel aground would show the same dayshape as a _________________.
Option_A: vessel towing a submerged object
Option_B: dredge underway and dredging
Option_C: hydrographic survey vessel at anchor and surveying
Correct_Answer: None of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway in fog when you hear a signal of three strokes of a bell, a rapid ringing of the bell, and three more strokes of the bell. This signal indicates a vessel __________________.
Option_A: at anchor, giving warning
Option_B: aground
Option_C: at anchor, greater than 100 meters
Correct_Answer: aground

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel "not under command" at night must show her sidelights when __________.
Option_A: making headway
Option_B: making no headway
Option_C: moored to a buoy
Correct_Answer: making headway

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The term "prolonged blast" means a blast of _________________.
Option_A: two to four seconds duration
Option_B: four to six seconds duration
Option_C: six to eight seconds duration
Correct_Answer: four to six seconds duration

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While you are underway,   navigation lights must be displayed on your vessel _____.
Option_A: during all periods of restricted visibility
Option_B: at all times
Option_C: at night only when other vessels may be in the area
Option_D: at night only when vessels are detected on radar
Correct_Answer: during all periods of restricted visibility

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning risk of collision?
Option_A: The stand-on vessel must keep out of the way of the other vessel when risk of collision exists.
Option_B: Risk of collision always exists when two vessels pass within one mile of each other.
Option_C: Risk of collision always exists when the compass bearing of an approaching vessel changes appreciably.
Option_D: Risk of collision may exist when the compass bearing of an approaching vessel is changing appreciably.
Correct_Answer: Risk of collision may exist when the compass bearing of an approaching vessel is changing appreciably.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel nearing a bend where other vessels may be obscured shall sound _______________.
Option_A: one short blast
Option_B: one long blast
Option_C: two short blasts
Correct_Answer: one prolonged blast

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel that is defined as  "restricted in her ability to maneuver" is unable to keep out of the way of another vessel due to ___________________.
Option_A: her draft
Option_B: the nature of her work
Option_C: some exceptional circumstances
Correct_Answer: the nature of her work

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway in fog, you hear a vessel sound four short blasts in succession. What does this signal indicate?
Option_A: A pilot vessel
Option_B: A vessel being towed
Option_C: A vessel fishing
Correct_Answer: A pilot vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are in charge of a stand-on vessel in a crossing situation. The other vessel is 1.5 miles to port. You believe that risk of collision exists. You should _____.
Option_A: take avoiding action immediately upon determining that risk of collision exists
Option_B: immediately sound the danger signal
Option_C: take avoiding action only after providing the give-way  vessel time to take action, and determining that her action is not appropriate
Option_D: hold course and speed until the point of extremis, and then sound the danger signal, taking whatever action will best avert collision
Correct_Answer: take avoiding action only after providing the give-way  vessel time to take action, and determining that her action is not appropriate

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In DIAGRAM 8, vessel "A" and vessel "B" (which is pushing ahead) are meeting head-on as shown. How must the vessels pass?
Option_A: Vessel "A" must alter course while vessel "B" continues on its present course.
Option_B: The vessels should determine which will alter course by  exchanging whistle signals.
Option_C: Both vessels should alter course to port and pass starboard to starboard.
Option_D: Both vessels should alter course to starboard and pass port to port.
Correct_Answer: Both vessels should alter course to starboard and pass port to port.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND To be considered "engaged in fishing" according to the Rules of the Road, a vessel must be ___________________.
Option_A: using fishing apparatus which restricts maneuverability
Option_B: using trolling lines
Option_C: power-driven
Option_D: showing lights or shapes for a vessel restricted in her  ability to maneuver
Correct_Answer: using fishing apparatus which restricts maneuverability

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway in fog you hear a rapid ringing of a bell ahead. This bell indicates a _____.
Option_A: vessel at anchor
Option_B: vessel in distress
Option_C: sailboat underway
Option_D: vessel backing out of a berth
Correct_Answer: vessel at anchor

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND An overtaking situation would be one in which one vessel is approaching another from more than how many degrees abaft the beam?
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A stand-on vessel is _____.
Option_A: required to give way in a crossing situation
Option_B: required to sound the first passing signal in a meeting  situation
Option_C: free to maneuver in any crossing or meeting situation as it has the right-of-way
Option_D: required to maintain course and speed in a crossing   situation but may take action to avoid collision
Correct_Answer: required to maintain course and speed in a crossing   situation but may take action to avoid collision

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND An overtaking situation at§night would be one in which one vessel sees which light(s)§of a vessel ahead?
Option_A: Masthead lights and sidelights
Option_B: One sidelight, the masthead lights and sternlight
Option_C: Both sidelights
Correct_Answer: Sternlight

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What lights must sailboats show when underway at night?
Option_A: One all-round white light
Option_B: A sternlight
Option_C: Red and green sidelights
Option_D: Red and green sidelights and a sternlight
Correct_Answer: Red and green sidelights and a sternlight

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are crossing a narrow  channel in a small motorboat. You sight a tankship off your port bow coming up the channel. Which statement is TRUE?
Option_A: You are the stand-on vessel because the tankship is to port.
Option_B: You cannot impede the safe passage of the tankship.
Option_C: The tankship is the stand-on vessel because it is to port of your vessel.
Option_D: The tankship is the stand-on vessel because it is the larger of the two vessels.
Correct_Answer: You cannot impede the safe passage of the tankship.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel does NOT sound a fog signal of one prolonged followed by two short blasts?
Option_A: A vessel dredging
Option_B: A vessel being towed
Option_C: A vessel engaged in fishing
Correct_Answer: A vessel being towed

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which light(s) is(are) AMONG those shown by a 200-meter vessel at anchor?
Option_A: In the forepart of the vessel, a 225° white light
Option_B: In the after part of the vessel, a 135° white light
Option_C: Any available working lights to illuminate the decks
Option_D: In the fore part of the vessel, a 135° white light
Correct_Answer: Any available working lights to illuminate the decks

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A partly submerged vessel or object being towed, which is not readily noticeable, shall show ___________________.
Option_A: yellow lights at each end
Option_B: two red lights in a vertical line
Option_C: a black ball
Correct_Answer: a diamond shape

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Concerning the identification §signal for a pilot vessel, in fog, which statement is TRUE?
Option_A: When at anchor, the pilot vessel is only required to sound anchor signals.
Option_B: The identification signal must be sounded any time the pilot vessel is underway.
Option_C: The pilot vessel may only sound the identity signal when making way.
Correct_Answer: When at anchor, the pilot vessel is only required to sound anchor signals.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In a crossing situation, a  vessel fishing must keep out of the way of a vessel which is ___________________.
Option_A: under sail
Option_B: towing
Option_C: restricted in her ability to maneuver
Correct_Answer: restricted in her ability to maneuver

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel would display a cone, apex downward?
Option_A: A fishing vessel with outlying gear
Option_B: A vessel proceeding under sail and machinery
Option_C: A vessel engaged in diving operations
Correct_Answer: A vessel proceeding under sail and machinery

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When action to avoid a close quarters situation is taken, a course change alone may be the most effective action provided that ________________.
Option_A: it is done in a succession of small course changes
Option_B: it is NOT done too early
Option_C: it is a large course change
Option_D: the course change is to starboard
Correct_Answer: it is a large course change

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway in heavy fog. You hear the fog signal of a vessel which is somewhere ahead of your vessel. You must _____.
Option_A: slow to moderate speed and navigate with caution
Option_B: maintain speed and sound the danger signal
Option_C: stop engines and navigate with caution
Option_D: slow to bare steerageway and navigate with caution
Correct_Answer: slow to bare steerageway and navigate with caution

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel at anchor will show a ____________________.
Option_A: ball
Option_B: cone
Option_C: cylinder
Correct_Answer: ball

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What dayshape must be shown by a vessel over 20 meters fishing which has gear extending more than 150 meters horizontally outward from it?
Option_A: One black ball
Option_B: One diamond shape
Option_C: One cone with its apex upwards
Correct_Answer: One cone with its apex upwards

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel towing astern   in an operation which severely restricts the towing vessel and her tow in their ability to change course shall, when making way, exhibit _________________.
Option_A: the masthead lights for a towing vessel
Option_B: the lights for a vessel restricted in its ability to  maneuver
Option_C: sidelights, sternlight and towing light
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel underway but not making way and fishing other than trawling will show which lights?
Option_A: A white light over a red light
Option_B: A red light over a white light
Option_C: A white light over a red light, sidelights, and a sternlight
Option_D: A red light over a white light, sidelights, and a sternlight
Correct_Answer: A red light over a white light

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 200-meter vessel is aground in restricted visibility. Which signal is optional?
Option_A: A bell signal
Option_B: A gong signal
Option_C: A whistle signal
Correct_Answer: A whistle signal

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel or object being towed astern shall display a(n) _____________________.
Option_A: forward masthead light
Option_B: after masthead light
Option_C: sternlight
Correct_Answer: sternlight

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The rules state that vessels may depart from the requirements of the Rules when ____________.
Option_A: there are no other vessels around
Option_B: operating in a narrow channel
Option_C: the Master enters it in the ship's log
Correct_Answer: necessary to avoid immediate danger

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND For the purpose of the Rules, except where otherwise required, the term _____.
Option_A: "vessel" includes seaplanes
Option_B: "seaplane" includes nondisplacement craft
Option_C: "vessel engaged in fishing" includes a vessel fishing with trolling lines
Option_D: "vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver" includes  fishing vessels
Correct_Answer: "vessel" includes seaplanes

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning a 75-meter power-driven vessel underway at night?
Option_A: She must exhibit an all-round white light at the stern.
Option_B: She must exhibit forward and after masthead lights.
Option_C: She must exhibit only a forward masthead light.
Option_D: She may exhibit a red light over a green light forward.
Correct_Answer: She must exhibit forward and after masthead lights.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Every vessel which is directed by these Rules to keep out of the way of another vessel  shall, if the circumstances of the case admit, avoid ______.
Option_A: crossing ahead of the other
Option_B: crossing astern of the other
Option_C: passing port to port
Correct_Answer: crossing ahead of the other

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which signal may be used by a vessel that is in doubt as to whether sufficient action is being taken by another vessel to avoid collision?
Option_A: A continuous sounding of the fog horn
Option_B: Firing a gun every minute
Option_C: Five or more short rapid blasts on the whistle
Option_D: One prolonged blast on the whistle
Correct_Answer: Five or more short rapid blasts on the whistle

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Navigation lights must be  displayed in all weathers from sunset to sunrise. They also _________________.
Option_A: must be displayed when day signals are being used
Option_B: must be displayed when moored to a pier
Option_C: may be extinguished at night on open waters when no other vessels are in the area
Correct_Answer: may be displayed during daylight

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What describes a head-on  situation?
Option_A: Seeing a vessel displaying both sidelights ONLY dead ahead
Option_B: Seeing two forward white towing identification lights in a vertical line on a towing vessel directly ahead
Option_C: Seeing both sidelights of a vessel directly off your  starboard beam
Option_D: Seeing both sidelights and masthead light(s) of a vessel dead ahead
Correct_Answer: Seeing both sidelights and masthead light(s) of a vessel dead ahead

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When two vessels are in   immediate danger of collision, the stand-on vessel must  _____________________.
Option_A: abandon ship
Option_B: assist in taking whatever action is necessary to avoid  collision
Option_C: hold course and speed
Correct_Answer: assist in taking whatever action is necessary to avoid  collision

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel 25 meters in length must have which sound signaling appliance onboard?
Option_A: None is required
Option_B: Whistle only
Option_C: Whistle and bell only
Correct_Answer: Whistle and bell only

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel transferring provisions or cargo at sea shall display during the day _____________.
Option_A: two black balls in a vertical line
Option_B: three black balls in a vertical line
Option_C: three shapes in a vertical line; the highest and lowest  shall be red balls and the middle a white diamond
Option_D: three black shapes in a vertical line; the highest and  lowest shall be balls and the middle one a diamond
Correct_Answer: three black shapes in a vertical line; the highest and  lowest shall be balls and the middle one a diamond

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You see a red sidelight bearing NW (315°). That vessel may be heading ___________.
Option_A: south (180°)
Option_B: east (090°)
Option_C: northeast (045°)
Correct_Answer: south (180°)

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Each prolonged blast on whistle§signals used by a power-driven vessel in fog, whether making§way or underway but not making way, is ____________.
Option_A: about one second
Option_B: two to four seconds
Option_C: four to six seconds
Correct_Answer: four to six seconds

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning a "vessel engaged in fishing"?
Option_A: The vessel may be using nets, lines, or trawls.
Option_B: The vessel may be trolling.
Option_C: The vessel shows 2 lights in a vertical line, white over red.
Option_D: The vessel sounds the same fog signal as a vessel underway, making no way.
Correct_Answer: The vessel may be using nets, lines, or trawls.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The Rules state that risk of collision shall be deemed to exist _____.
Option_A: whenever two vessels approach from opposite directions
Option_B: if the bearing of an approaching vessel does not appreciably change
Option_C: whenever a vessel crosses ahead of the intended track of another vessel
Option_D: if one vessel approaches another so as to be overtaking
Correct_Answer: if the bearing of an approaching vessel does not appreciably change

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel exhibits the same lights as a ________________.
Option_A: vessel towing, when not underway
Option_B: vessel towing astern
Option_C: sailing vessel
Option_D: pushing vessel and a vessel being pushed, when they are in a composite unit
Correct_Answer: pushing vessel and a vessel being pushed, when they are in a composite unit

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel is  underway in fog but stopped and making no way through the water. What is the required fog signal?
Option_A: One prolonged blast at not more than one-minute intervals
Option_B: Two prolonged blasts at not more than one-minute intervals
Option_C: One prolonged blast at not more than two-minute intervals
Option_D: Two prolonged blasts at not more than two-minute intervals
Correct_Answer: Two prolonged blasts at not more than two-minute intervals

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A towing light, according to§the Rules, is a _______________.
Option_A: white light
Option_B: red light
Option_C: yellow light
Correct_Answer: yellow light

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which signal shall a   power-driven vessel sound when making way in fog?
Option_A: One short blast every two minutes
Option_B: One prolonged blast every two minutes
Option_C: One prolonged and two short blasts every two minutes
Option_D: Three short blasts every two minutes
Correct_Answer: One prolonged blast every two minutes

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Two vessels are meeting head-on. How must the vessels pass?
Option_A: One vessel must alter course while the other must continue on its course.
Option_B: The vessels should determine which will alter course by  sounding whistle signals.
Option_C: Both vessels should alter course to port and pass starboard to starboard.
Option_D: Both vessels should alter course to starboard and pass port to port.
Correct_Answer: Both vessels should alter course to starboard and pass port to port.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel does NOT sound a fog signal of one prolonged followed by two short blasts?
Option_A: A vessel engaged in dredging
Option_B: A sailing vessel
Option_C: A vessel being towed
Correct_Answer: A vessel being towed

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel 50 meters in length at anchor must sound which fog signal?
Option_A: 5-second ringing of a bell every minute
Option_B: 5-second ringing of a bell every two minutes
Option_C: 5-second sounding of a gong every minute
Option_D: 5-second sounding of both a bell and gong every two minutes
Correct_Answer: 5-second ringing of a bell every minute

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel is NOT to be  regarded as "restricted in her ability to maneuver"?
Option_A: A vessel transferring provisions while underway
Option_B: A pushing vessel and a vessel being pushed when connected in a composite unit
Option_C: A vessel servicing a navigation mark
Correct_Answer: A pushing vessel and a vessel being pushed when connected in a composite unit

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement correctly  applies to a situation where a sailing vessel is overtaking a power-driven vessel?
Option_A: The power-driven vessel must keep out of the way of the  sailing vessel.
Option_B: A "special circumstance" situation exists.
Option_C: The sailing vessel must keep out of the way of the power- driven vessel.
Option_D: The vessel which has the other vessel to the right must keep out of the way.
Correct_Answer: The sailing vessel must keep out of the way of the power- driven vessel.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which procedure(s) shall be used to determine risk of collision?
Option_A: Watching the compass bearing of an approaching vessel
Option_B: Systematic observation of objects detected by radar
Option_C: Long-range radar scanning
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A white masthead light shows through an arc of how many degrees?
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is the minimum length of an anchored vessel which is required to show a white light both forward and aft?
Option_A: 50 meters
Option_B: 100 meters
Option_C: 150 meters
Correct_Answer: 50 meters

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are at anchor in fog. §The fog signal of a vessel underway has been steadily§growing louder and the danger of collision appears to exist.§In addition to your fog signal, what signal may be used§to indicate the presence of your vessel?
Option_A: Three blasts on the whiste; one prolonged, one short, and one prolonged.
Option_B: Three blasts on the whistle; one short, one prolonged, and one short.
Option_C: Three blasts on the whistle; one prolonged followed by two short.
Option_D: No signal other than your fog signal may be used.
Correct_Answer: Three blasts on the whistle; one short, one prolonged, and one short.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Signals required for vessels aground include _________________.
Option_A: by night, the anchor lights for a vessel of her length, and three red lights in a vertical line
Option_B: a short, a prolonged, and a short blast
Option_C: by day, three black balls in a vertical line
Correct_Answer: by day, three black balls in a vertical line

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which craft would be considered a "power-driven vessel" under the Rules of the Road?
Option_A: An auxiliary sail vessel, using her engine
Option_B: A canoe being propelled by a small outboard motor
Option_C: A tug powered by a diesel engine
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND At night, power-driven vessels less than 12 meters in length may, instead of the underway lights for vessels under 50 meters, show which lights?
Option_A: Sidelights and sternlight
Option_B: One all-round white light and sidelights
Option_C: Masthead light only
Correct_Answer: One all-round white light and sidelights

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel shall not impede the passage of a vessel which can only navigate inside a narrow channel?
Option_A: A vessel of less than 20 meters in length
Option_B: A vessel not under command
Option_C: A vessel engaged in surveying
Correct_Answer: A vessel of less than 20 meters in length

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE in  an overtaking situation?
Option_A: One vessel is approaching another vessel from more than 20° abaft the beam.
Option_B: It is the duty of the vessel being overtaken to get out of the way.
Option_C: Any later change of bearing between the two vessels shall not make the overtaking vessel a crossing vessel.
Correct_Answer: Any later change of bearing between the two vessels shall not make the overtaking vessel a crossing vessel.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel must exhibit a  conical shape, apex downwards?
Option_A: A 10-meter vessel engaged in fishing
Option_B: A 15-meter vessel proceeding under sail when also being  propelled by machinery
Option_C: A 20-meter vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver
Correct_Answer: A 15-meter vessel proceeding under sail when also being  propelled by machinery

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel must show a towing light above the sternlight?
Option_A: A vessel pushing three barges ahead
Option_B: A vessel towing alongside
Option_C: A vessel with a 150-meter tow astern
Correct_Answer: A vessel with a 150-meter tow astern

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which is NOT a distress signal?
Option_A: A continuous sounding with any fog signal apparatus
Option_B: A signal sent by radiotelephone consisting of the spoken word "Mayday"
Option_C: An International Code Signal of N.C.
Option_D: The firing of green star rockets or shells
Correct_Answer: The firing of green star rockets or shells

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A rigid replica of the   International Code flag "A" may be shown by a vessel  _____________________.
Option_A: pulling a submarine cable
Option_B: engaged in diving operations
Option_C: engaged in underway replenishment
Correct_Answer: engaged in diving operations

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In a crossing situation, which vessel may sound the danger signal?
Option_A: Give-way vessel
Option_B: Stand-on vessel
Option_C: Either vessel
Correct_Answer: Either vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Every vessel should at all times proceed at a "safe speed". "Safe speed" is defined as that speed where _____.
Option_A: you can stop within your visibility range
Option_B: you can take proper and effective action to avoid collision
Option_C: you are traveling slower than surrounding vessels
Option_D: no wake comes from your vessel
Correct_Answer: you can take proper and effective action to avoid collision

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway in fog and you hear three distinct bell strokes followed by five seconds of rapid bell ringing followed by three distinct bell strokes. This signal indicates a vessel _________________.
Option_A: aground
Option_B: engaged in underwater construction
Option_C: at anchor
Correct_Answer: aground

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In a crossing situation,a stand-on vessel which is forced to take action in order§to avoid collision with a vessel on her own port side shall, if possible, avoid _____________________.
Option_A: turning to port
Option_B: turning to starboard
Option_C: decreasing speed
Correct_Answer: turning to port

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel is "underway"  within the meaning of the Rules?
Option_A: A vessel at anchor with the engine turning
Option_B: A vessel tied to an offshore mooring buoy
Option_C: A vessel aground with the engine turning
Option_D: A vessel drifting with the engine stopped
Correct_Answer: A vessel drifting with the engine stopped

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is the required fog signal for a manned vessel being towed at night?
Option_A: One prolonged followed by one short blast
Option_B: One prolonged followed by three short blasts
Option_C: One prolonged followed by two short blasts
Correct_Answer: One prolonged followed by three short blasts

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If you anchor your 25-meter  vessel in a harbor, what light(s) must you show?
Option_A: One all-round white light
Option_B: Two all-round white lights
Option_C: One all-round red light
Correct_Answer: One all-round white light

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Three short blasts of the  whistle means _______________.
Option_A: "danger"
Option_B: "I am in distress"
Option_C: "my vessel is towing"
Correct_Answer: "I am operating astern propulsion"

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Of the vessels listed, which must keep out of the way of all the others?
Option_A: A sailing vessel
Option_B: A vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver
Option_C: A vessel not under command
Correct_Answer: A sailing vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND During the day, a vessel with a tow over 200 meters in length will show _________________.
Option_A: a black ball
Option_B: a diamond shape
Option_C: two cones, apexes together
Correct_Answer: a diamond shape

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A fog signal of one prolonged blast followed by four short blasts would mean the presence of a ________________.
Option_A: vessel being towed
Option_B: fishing vessel trawling
Option_C: vessel at anchor warning of her location
Option_D: power-driven pilot vessel on station underway
Correct_Answer: power-driven pilot vessel on station underway

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel not under command,  underway but not making way, would show ___________________.
Option_A: two all-round red lights in a vertical line
Option_B: sidelights
Option_C: a sternlight
Correct_Answer: two all-round red lights in a vertical line

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Traffic separation schemes ______________________________.
Option_A: provide routing and scheduling procedures to reduce shipping delays
Option_B: provide traffic patterns in congested areas, so that vessels can operate without having a separate lookout
Option_C: provide inbound and outbound lanes to promote the safe flow of vessel traffic
Option_D: prohibit vessels carrying hazardous cargoes from entering waters that are environmentally sensitive
Correct_Answer: provide inbound and outbound lanes to promote the safe flow of vessel traffic

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which lights shall a 200-meter vessel exhibit when at anchor?
Option_A: In the forepart of the vessel, a 225-degree white light
Option_B: In the after part of the vessel, a 112.5-degree white light
Option_C: Working lights to illuminate the decks
Option_D: In the forepart of the vessel, a 112.5-degree white light
Correct_Answer: Working lights to illuminate the decks

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Under the Rules, the term  "vessel" includes _____.
Option_A: non-self-propelled raft
Option_B: seaplanes
Option_C: hovercrafts
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You see a vessel displaying  three lights in a vertical line. The highest and lowest lights are red and the middle light is white. She is also showing a white light at the stern, which is lower than the forward light. It could be a _________________.
Option_A: survey vessel
Option_B: vessel not under command
Option_C: vessel aground
Option_D: pilot vessel with port side to you
Correct_Answer: survey vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A pilot vessel may continue to sound an identity signal in fog if she is _______________.
Option_A: aground
Option_B: at anchor
Option_C: not under command
Correct_Answer: at anchor

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are in charge of a stand-on vessel in a crossing situation. The other vessel is 1.5 miles to port. You believe that risk of collision exists. You should _____.
Option_A: take avoiding action immediately upon determining that risk of collision exists
Option_B: immediately sound the danger signal, and change course
Option_C: take avoiding action only after giving the give-way vessel time to take action, and determining that her action is not appropriate
Option_D: hold course and speed until the point of extremis, and then sound the danger signal, taking whatever action will best avoid collision
Correct_Answer: take avoiding action only after giving the give-way vessel time to take action, and determining that her action is not appropriate

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel towing astern   in an operation which severely restricts the towing vessel and her tow in their ability to deviate from their course shall, when making way, show _________________.
Option_A: the masthead lights for a towing vessel
Option_B: the lights for a vessel restricted in its ability to  maneuver
Option_C: sidelights, sternlight and towing light
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning seaplanes on the water?
Option_A: A seaplane must exhibit appropriate lights but need not  exhibit shapes.
Option_B: A seaplane should show the lights for a vessel constrained by her draft.
Option_C: In situations where a risk of collision exists, a seaplane should always give way.
Option_D: A seaplane on the water shall, in general, keep well clear of all vessels.
Correct_Answer: A seaplane on the water shall, in general, keep well clear of all vessels.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A head-on situation at night is one in which you see dead ahead a vessel showing _______________.
Option_A: one sidelight
Option_B: one sidelight and a masthead light
Option_C: one sidelight and two masthead lights
Option_D: both sidelights of a vessel and her masthead light(s)
Correct_Answer: both sidelights of a vessel and her masthead light(s)

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In a crossing situation, the stand-on vessel should normally _____.
Option_A: take action to cross ahead of the other vessel
Option_B: take action to pass astern of the other vessel
Option_C: maintain course and speed
Correct_Answer: maintain course and speed

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A self-propelled dredge not engaged in dredging but proceeding to a dredging location at night would ______.
Option_A: not be required to show any lights
Option_B: be required to show the lights characteristic of a dredge
Option_C: be required to show the lights of a stationary dredge
Option_D: be required to show the lights of a power-driven vessel  underway
Correct_Answer: be required to show the lights of a power-driven vessel  underway

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND At night you sight a vessel  displaying one green light. This light could indicate a _________________.
Option_A: vessel drifting
Option_B: vessel at anchor
Option_C: small motorboat underway
Correct_Answer: sailboat underway

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND There is a provision to depart from the Rules, if necessary, to avoid _________________.
Option_A: a close-quarters situation
Option_B: an overtaking situation
Option_C: immediate danger
Correct_Answer: immediate danger

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Risk of collision exists when an approaching vessel has a(n) _____.
Option_A: generally steady bearing and decreasing range
Option_B: generally steady range and increasing bearing
Option_C: increasing range and bearing
Correct_Answer: generally steady bearing and decreasing range

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What signal indicates doubt that sufficient action is being taken by another vessel to avoid collision?
Option_A: Five short and rapid blasts of the whistle
Option_B: Three long blasts of the whistle
Option_C: Three short and rapid blasts of the whistle
Option_D: One prolonged blast followed by three short blasts of the whistle
Correct_Answer: Five short and rapid blasts of the whistle

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel towing another vessel astern (tow less than 200 meters) shall show _________________.
Option_A: a small white light abaft the funnel
Option_B: three masthead lights in a vertical line instead of either the forward or after masthead lights
Option_C: two masthead lights in a vertical line instead of either the forward or after masthead lights
Option_D: two towing lights in a vertical line at the stern
Correct_Answer: two masthead lights in a vertical line instead of either the forward or after masthead lights

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway in fog, you hear§the rapid ringing of a bell for about five seconds followed§by the sounding of a gong for about five seconds. This §signal came from a __________.
Option_A: vessel engaged in fishing at anchor
Option_B: sailing vessel at anchor
Option_C: vessel 150 meters in length at anchor
Correct_Answer: vessel 150 meters in length at anchor

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway in a narrow channel and you are being overtaken by a vessel astern. The overtaking vessel sounds a signal indicating his intention to pass your vessel on your starboard side. If such an  action appears dangerous you should sound _______________.
Option_A: five short and rapid blasts
Option_B: three short and rapid blasts
Option_C: one prolonged followed by one short blast
Option_D: one prolonged, one short, one prolonged, and one short blast in that order
Correct_Answer: five short and rapid blasts

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel restricted in her  ability to maneuver shall _____________________.
Option_A: turn off her sidelights when not making way
Option_B: when operating in restricted visibility, sound a whistle signal of two prolonged and one short blast
Option_C: show a dayshape of two diamonds in a vertical line
Option_D: keep out of the way of a vessel engaged in fishing
Correct_Answer: turn off her sidelights when not making way

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel at anchor,§not fishing or otherwise restricted in its ability to§maneuver, sounds her fog signal at intervals of not _______.
Option_A: more than one minute
Option_B: more than two minutes
Option_C: more than three minutes
Correct_Answer: more than one minute

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway in reduced§visibility. You hear the fog signal of another vessel about§20° on your starboard bow. Risk of collision may exist.§You should _________.
Option_A: alter course to starboard to pass around the other vessel
Option_B: reduce your speed to bare steerageway
Option_C: slow your engines and let the other vessel pass ahead of you
Option_D: alter course to port to pass the other vessel on its portside
Correct_Answer: reduce your speed to bare steerageway

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What dayshape would a vessel at anchor show during daylight?
Option_A: One black ball
Option_B: Two black balls
Option_C: Three black balls
Correct_Answer: One black ball

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are approaching a bend in a channel. You cannot see around the bend because of the  height of the bank. You should _______________.
Option_A: stop engines and navigate with caution
Option_B: stay in the middle of the channel
Option_C: sound passing signals to any other vessel that may be on the other side of the bend
Option_D: sound a whistle blast of 4 to 6 seconds duration
Correct_Answer: sound a whistle blast of 4 to 6 seconds duration

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning a vessel of 150 meters in length, at anchor?
Option_A: She may show an all-round white light where it can best be seen.
Option_B: She must show an all-round white light forward and a second such light aft.
Option_C: The showing of working lights is optional.
Correct_Answer: She must show an all-round white light forward and a second such light aft.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel would be required to show a white light from a lantern exhibited in sufficient time to prevent collision?
Option_A: A 9-meter sailing vessel
Option_B: A rowboat
Option_C: A 6-meter motorboat
Correct_Answer: A rowboat

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Barges being towed at night  ___________________.
Option_A: must be lighted at all times
Option_B: must be lighted only if manned
Option_C: must be lighted only if towed astern
Correct_Answer: must be lighted at all times

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You sight another power-driven§vessel dead-ahead showing both the red and green sidelights.§ The required action to take would be to ____________.
Option_A: carefully watch his compass bearing
Option_B: start a radar plot in order to ascertain his course
Option_C: alter your course to port
Correct_Answer: alter your course to starboard

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway in fog and hear one short, one prolonged, and one short blast in succession. What is the meaning of this signal?
Option_A: A vessel is in distress and needs assistance.
Option_B: A vessel is fishing, hauling nets.
Option_C: A vessel is at anchor, warning of her position.
Correct_Answer: A vessel is at anchor, warning of her position.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND An anchored vessel on pilotage §duty must show which light(s) at night?
Option_A: A sternlight only
Option_B: Anchor lights only
Option_C: A white light over a red light only
Option_D: A white light over a red light and anchor lights
Correct_Answer: A white light over a red light and anchor lights

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel which is fishing is required to show sidelights and a sternlight only when  ____________________.
Option_A: anchored
Option_B: underway
Option_C: dead in the water
Correct_Answer: underway and making way

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is a requirement for any action taken to avoid collision?
Option_A: When in sight of another vessel, any action taken must be accompanied by sound signals.
Option_B: The action taken must include changing the speed of the  vessel.
Option_C: The action must be positive and made in ample time.
Correct_Answer: The action must be positive and made in ample time.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In the daytime, you see a large sailing vessel on the beam. You know that she is also  propelled by machinery if she shows _________________.
Option_A: a basket
Option_B: a black ball
Option_C: a black cone
Correct_Answer: a black cone

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your vessel is stopped and  making no way, but is not in any way disabled. Another  vessel is approaching you on your starboard beam. Which statement is TRUE?
Option_A: The other vessel must give way since your vessel is stopped.
Option_B: Your vessel is the give-way vessel in a crossing situation.
Option_C: You should be showing the lights or shapes for a vessel not under command.
Option_D: You should be showing the lights or shapes for a vessel  restricted in her ability to maneuver.
Correct_Answer: Your vessel is the give-way vessel in a crossing situation.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND For identification purposes at night, U.S. Navy submarines on the surface may display an intermittent flashing light of which color?
Option_A: Amber (yellow)
Option_B: White
Option_C: Blue
Correct_Answer: Amber (yellow)

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Vessels engaged in fishing may show the additional signals described in Annex II to the Rules when they are ______________.
Option_A: trolling
Option_B: fishing in a traffic separation zone
Option_C: in a narrow channel
Option_D: in close proximity to other vessels engaged in fishing
Correct_Answer: in close proximity to other vessels engaged in fishing

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel must show a  masthead light abaft of and higher than her identifying  lights?
Option_A: A 55-meter vessel fishing
Option_B: A 55-meter vessel trawling
Option_C: A 100-meter vessel not under command
Option_D: A 20-meter vessel engaged on pilotage duty
Correct_Answer: A 55-meter vessel trawling

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway in a narrow  channel, a vessel should stay _____.
Option_A: in the middle of the channel
Option_B: to the starboard side of the channel
Option_C: to the port side of the channel
Option_D: to the side of the channel that has the widest bends
Correct_Answer: to the starboard side of the channel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Vessels of less than what length may not impede the passage of other vessels in a narrow  fairway?
Option_A: 10 meters
Option_B: 20 meters
Option_C: 30 meters
Correct_Answer: 20 meters

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A lantern combining§the sidelights and sternlight MAY be shown on a __________.
Option_A: sailing vessel of 25 meters in length
Option_B: 20-meter vessel engaged in fishing and making way
Option_C: 25-meter power-driven vessel engaged in trolling
Correct_Answer: 6-meter vessel under oars

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The lights required by the Rules must be shown _____.
Option_A: from sunrise to sunset in restricted visibility
Option_B: at all times
Option_C: ONLY from sunset to sunrise
Correct_Answer: from sunrise to sunset in restricted visibility

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel may carry her  sidelights and sternlight in a combined lantern on the mast?
Option_A: An 18-meter sailing vessel
Option_B: A 10-meter sailing vessel also being propelled by machinery
Option_C: A 25-meter sailing vessel
Correct_Answer: An 18-meter sailing vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel nearing a bend or§an area of a channel or fairway where other vessels may§be hidden by an obstruction shall _____.
Option_A: sound the danger signal
Option_B: sound a prolonged blast
Option_C: take all way off
Correct_Answer: sound a prolonged blast

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are approaching a vessel dredging during the day and see two balls in a vertical line on the port side of the dredge. These shapes mean that  ________________.
Option_A: you should pass on the port side of the dredge
Option_B: there is an obstruction on the port side of the dredge
Option_C: the dredge is not under command
Correct_Answer: there is an obstruction on the port side of the dredge

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning the light used to accompany whistle signals?
Option_A: It is mandatory to use such a light.
Option_B: The light shall have the same characteristics as a masthead light.
Option_C: It is used to supplement short blasts of the whistle.
Correct_Answer: It is used to supplement short blasts of the whistle.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel must sound her fog signal at intervals not to exceed one minute?
Option_A: A power-driven vessel underway, not making way
Option_B: A vessel constrained by her draft
Option_C: A vessel engaged in fishing, at anchor
Correct_Answer: A vessel aground

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND By day, you sight a vessel  displaying three shapes in a vertical line. The top and bottom shapes are balls, and the middle shape is a diamond. It could be a __________________.
Option_A: vessel trolling
Option_B: mineclearing vessel
Option_C: trawler
Option_D: vessel engaged in replenishment at sea
Correct_Answer: vessel engaged in replenishment at sea

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are heading due east (090°) and observe a vessel's red sidelight on your port beam. The vessel may be heading _____.
Option_A: northwest (315°)
Option_B: north  (000°)
Option_C: southeast (135°)
Correct_Answer: southwest (225°)

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel is, by definition, unable to keep out of the way of another vessel?
Option_A: Vessel engaged in fishing
Option_B: Vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver
Option_C: Sailing vessel
Correct_Answer: Vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel must exhibit  forward and after masthead lights when underway?
Option_A: A 200-meter sailing vessel
Option_B: A 50-meter power-driven vessel
Option_C: A 100-meter vessel engaged in fishing
Correct_Answer: A 50-meter power-driven vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND As defined in the Rules, a  towing light is a yellow light having the same    characteristics as a(n) ____________.
Option_A: masthead light
Option_B: all-round light
Option_C: sidelight
Correct_Answer: sternlight

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel underway and making way in fog shall sound every two minutes ___________________.
Option_A: one prolonged blast
Option_B: two prolonged blasts
Option_C: one prolonged blast and three short blasts
Correct_Answer: one prolonged blast

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When anchoring a 20-meter vessel at night, you must show _________________.
Option_A: one all-round white light
Option_B: two all-round white lights
Option_C: one all-round white light and the sternlight
Option_D: one all-round white light and a flare up light
Correct_Answer: one all-round white light

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND According to the Navigation  Rules, all of the following are engaged in fishing EXCEPT a vessel ___________________.
Option_A: setting nets
Option_B: trawling
Option_C: using a dredge net
Correct_Answer: trolling

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When a vessel sounds three short blasts on the whistle, this indicates that ______________.
Option_A: danger is ahead
Option_B: her engines are going astern
Option_C: the vessel is not under command (broken down)
Option_D: all other vessels should stand clear
Correct_Answer: her engines are going astern

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel is overtaking when she approaches another from more than how many degrees abaft the beam?
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What equipment for fog signals is required for a vessel 20 meters in length?
Option_A: Whistle only
Option_B: Bell only
Option_C: Whistle and bell only
Correct_Answer: Whistle and bell only

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Sailing vessels are stand-on over power-driven vessels except __________________.
Option_A: in a crossing situation
Option_B: in a meeting situation
Option_C: when they are the overtaking vessel
Option_D: on the inland waters of the U.S.
Correct_Answer: when they are the overtaking vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning risk of collision?
Option_A: Risk of collision never exists if the compass bearing of the other vessel is changing.
Option_B: Proper use shall be made of radar equipment to determine risk of collision.
Option_C: Risk of collision must be determined before any action can be taken by a vessel.
Option_D: Risk of collision exists if the vessels will pass within half a mile of each other.
Correct_Answer: Proper use shall be made of radar equipment to determine risk of collision.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are fishing at night, and you sight a vessel showing three lights in a vertical line. The upper and lower lights are red and the middle light is white. Which statement is TRUE?
Option_A: You must keep out of the way of the other vessel.
Option_B: The other vessel is responsible to keep out of your way.
Option_C: The other vessel is at anchor.
Option_D: The rule of special circumstances applies.
Correct_Answer: You must keep out of the way of the other vessel.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel is to sound a fog signal of one prolonged followed by two short blasts?
Option_A: A vessel not under command
Option_B: A sailing vessel, underway
Option_C: A vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver when carrying out her work at anchor
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel may exhibit lights  other than those prescribed by the Rules as long as the  additional lights _____.
Option_A: do not interfere with the keeping of a proper look-out
Option_B: are not the color of either sidelight
Option_C: have a lesser range than the prescribed lights
Correct_Answer: do not interfere with the keeping of a proper look-out

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning a partly submerged vessel being towed?
Option_A: It must show a yellow light at each end.
Option_B: It will show red lights along its length.
Option_C: A diamond shape will be carried at the aftermost extremity of the tow.
Correct_Answer: A diamond shape will be carried at the aftermost extremity of the tow.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your vessel enters fog. You stop your engines, and the vessel is dead in the water.  Which fog signal should you sound?
Option_A: One prolonged blast every two minutes
Option_B: Two prolonged blasts every two minutes
Option_C: Three short blasts every two minutes
Option_D: One prolonged and two short blasts every two minutes
Correct_Answer: Two prolonged blasts every two minutes

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The term "power-driven vessel" refers to any vessel _________________.
Option_A: with propelling machinery onboard whether in use or not
Option_B: making way against the current
Option_C: with propelling machinery in use
Option_D: travelling at a speed greater than that of the current
Correct_Answer: with propelling machinery in use

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In which situation do the Rules require both vessels to change course?
Option_A: Two power-driven vessels meeting head-on
Option_B: Two power-driven vessels crossing when it is apparent to the stand-on vessel that the give-way vessel is not taking  appropriate action
Option_C: Two sailing vessels crossing with the wind on the same side
Correct_Answer: Two power-driven vessels meeting head-on

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel towing where the tow prevents her from changing course shall carry _____________.
Option_A: only the lights for a vessel towing
Option_B: only the lights for a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver
Option_C: the lights for a towing vessel and the lights for a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver
Option_D: the lights for a towing vessel and the lights for a vessel not under command
Correct_Answer: the lights for a towing vessel and the lights for a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning the danger signal?
Option_A: May be sounded by the stand-on vessel only
Option_B: Indicates that the vessel is in distress
Option_C: Is used to indicate a course change
Option_D: May be supplemented by an appropriate light signal
Correct_Answer: May be supplemented by an appropriate light signal

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If a sailing vessel with the wind on the port side sees a sailing vessel to windward and cannot tell whether the other vessel has the wind on the port or starboard side, she shall __________________.
Option_A: hold course and speed
Option_B: sound the danger signal
Option_C: keep out of the way of the other vessel
Option_D: turn to port and come into the wind
Correct_Answer: keep out of the way of the other vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Vessel "A" is on course 000° T. Vessel "B" is on a course such that she is involved in a head-on situation and is bearing 355° T, 2 miles away from vessel "A". To ensure a safe passing, vessel "A" should ________________.
Option_A: maintain course
Option_B: alter course to port
Option_C: alter course to ensure a starboard to starboard passing
Option_D: maneuver to ensure a port to port passing
Correct_Answer: maneuver to ensure a port to port passing

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is a vessel "restricted in her ability to maneuver"?
Option_A: A vessel not under command
Option_B: A vessel constrained by her draft
Option_C: A vessel underway in fog
Option_D: A vessel towing unable to deviate from her course
Correct_Answer: A vessel towing unable to deviate from her course

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND All of the following are  distress signals under the Rules EXCEPT ___________________.
Option_A: a green star signal
Option_B: orange-colored smoke
Option_C: red flares
Option_D: the repeated raising and lowering of outstretched arms
Correct_Answer: a green star signal

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The Rules state that vessels may depart from the Rules when _________________.
Option_A: there are no other vessels around
Option_B: operating in a narrow channel
Option_C: the Master enters it in the ship's log
Correct_Answer: necessary to avoid immediate danger

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel is towing and carrying the required lights on the masthead. What is the visibility arc of these lights?
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which situation would be a  "special circumstance" under the Rules?
Option_A: Vessel at anchor
Option_B: More than two vessels meeting
Option_C: Speed in fog
Correct_Answer: More than two vessels meeting

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are approaching another  vessel on crossing courses. She is approximately half a mile distant and is presently on your starboard bow. You believe she will cross ahead of you. She then sounds a  whistle signal of five short blasts. You should __________.
Option_A: answer the signal and hold course and speed
Option_B: reduce speed slightly to make sure she will have room to pass
Option_C: make a large course change, accompanied by the appropriate whistle signal, and slow down if necessary
Option_D: wait for another whistle signal from the other vessel
Correct_Answer: make a large course change, accompanied by the appropriate whistle signal, and slow down if necessary

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are approaching another vessel and are not sure whether danger of collision exists. You must assume ______________.
Option_A: there is risk of collision
Option_B: you are the give way vessel
Option_C: the other vessel is also in doubt
Option_D: All of the above are correct.
Correct_Answer: there is risk of collision

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel may use the danger signal?
Option_A: The vessel to starboard when two power-driven vessels are  crossing
Option_B: A vessel engaged in fishing, crossing the course of a  sailing vessel
Option_C: Either of two power-driven vessels meeting head-on
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is the minimum sound  signaling equipment required aboard a vessel 10 meters in length?
Option_A: A bell only
Option_B: A whistle only
Option_C: A bell and a whistle
Option_D: Any means of making an efficient sound signal
Correct_Answer: Any means of making an efficient sound signal

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   regarding equipment for sound signals?
Option_A: A vessel of less than 12 meters in length need not have any sound signaling equipment.
Option_B: Any vessel over 12 meters in length must be provided with a gong.
Option_C: Manual sounding of the signals must always be possible.
Option_D: Automatic sounding of the signals is not permitted.
Correct_Answer: Manual sounding of the signals must always be possible.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement concerning an overtaking situation is correct?
Option_A: The overtaking vessel is the stand-on vessel.
Option_B: Neither vessel is the stand-on vessel.
Option_C: The overtaking vessel must maintain course and speed.
Option_D: The overtaking vessel must keep out of the way of the other.
Correct_Answer: The overtaking vessel must keep out of the way of the other.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The Rules state that a vessel overtaking another vessel is relieved of her duty to keep clear when __________________.
Option_A: she is forward of the other vessel's beam
Option_B: the overtaking situation becomes a crossing situation
Option_C: she is past and clear of the other vessel
Option_D: the other vessel is no longer in sight
Correct_Answer: she is past and clear of the other vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is§TRUE concerning fog signals?
Option_A: All fog signals for sailing vessels are to be given at intervals of not more than one minute.
Option_B: A vessel not under command sounds the same fog signal as a vessel towed.
Option_C: A pilot vessel underway and making way sounds the pilot identity signal and no other signal.
Option_D: A vessel aground may sound a whistle signal.
Correct_Answer: A vessel aground may sound a whistle signal.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which dayshape would a vessel aground show during daylight?
Option_A: One black ball
Option_B: Two black balls
Option_C: Three black balls
Correct_Answer: Three black balls

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel must have a gong, or other equipment which will make the sound of a gong?
Option_A: A sailing vessel
Option_B: Any vessel over 50 meters
Option_C: Any vessel over 100 meters
Correct_Answer: Any vessel over 100 meters

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A sailing vessel is proceeding along a narrow channel and can safely navigate ONLY inside the channel. The sailing vessel approaches a vessel engaged in fishing. Which statement is TRUE?
Option_A: The fishing vessel is directed not to impede the passage of the sailing vessel.
Option_B: The sailing vessel must keep out of the way of the fishing vessel.
Option_C: Each vessel should move to the edge of the channel on her port side.
Option_D: Each vessel should be displaying signals for a vessel  constrained by her draft.
Correct_Answer: The fishing vessel is directed not to impede the passage of the sailing vessel.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Dayshapes MUST be shown ______.
Option_A: during daylight hours
Option_B: during daylight hours except in restricted visibility
Option_C: ONLY between 8 AM and 4 PM daily
Correct_Answer: during daylight hours

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Rule 14 describes the action to be taken by vessels meeting head-on. Which of the  following conditions must exist in order for this rule to apply?
Option_A: Both vessels must be power-driven.
Option_B: They must be meeting on reciprocal or nearly reciprocal  courses.
Option_C: The situation must involve risk of collision.
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The sternlight shall be   positioned such that it will show from dead astern to how many degrees on each side of the stern of the vessel?
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel aground at night is required to show two red lights in a vertical line as well as _____.
Option_A: not under command lights
Option_B: restricted in her ability to maneuver lights
Option_C: anchor lights
Correct_Answer: anchor lights

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When towing more than one barge astern at night _______________.
Option_A: only the last barge on the tow must be lighted
Option_B: only the first and the last barges in the tow must be  lighted
Option_C: each barge in the tow must be lighted
Option_D: only manned barges must be lighted
Correct_Answer: each barge in the tow must be lighted

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your vessel is aground in fog. In addition to the regular anchor signals, you will be  sounding _______________.
Option_A: three strokes of the gong before and after the rapid ringing of the gong
Option_B: a blast on the whistle
Option_C: three strokes of the bell before and after the rapid ringing of the bell
Correct_Answer: three strokes of the bell before and after the rapid ringing of the bell

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In a crossing situation, the vessel which has the other on her own starboard side shall ___________________.
Option_A: if the circumstances of the case admit, avoid crossing ahead of the other
Option_B: change course to port to keep out of the way
Option_C: reduce her speed
Correct_Answer: if the circumstances of the case admit, avoid crossing ahead of the other

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are on vessel "A" in  DIAGRAM 32, and hear vessel "B" sound a signal indicating her intention to overtake you. You feel it is not safe for vessel "B" to overtake you at the present time. You should ___________________.
Option_A: sound five or more short rapid blasts
Option_B: sound two short blasts
Option_C: not answer the whistle signal from vessel "B"
Option_D: sound three blasts of the whistle
Correct_Answer: sound five or more short rapid blasts

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel sounds the same fog signal when underway or at anchor?
Option_A: A sailing vessel
Option_B: A vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver
Option_C: A vessel constrained by her draft
Correct_Answer: A vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are approaching a bend in a river where, due to the bank, you cannot see around the  other side. A vessel on the other side of the bend sounds one prolonged blast. You should ___________________.
Option_A: sound passing signals
Option_B: not sound any signal until you sight the other vessel
Option_C: sound a prolonged blast
Correct_Answer: sound a prolonged blast

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In DIAGRAM 5, vessel "A", which is pushing ahead, and vessel "B" are crossing. Which is the stand-on vessel?
Option_A: Vessel "A" is the stand-on vessel because she is to port of vessel "B".
Option_B: Vessel "A" is the stand-on vessel because she is pushing ahead.
Option_C: Vessel "B" is the stand-on vessel because she is to   starboard of vessel "A".
Option_D: Neither vessel is the stand-on vessel in this situation.
Correct_Answer: Vessel "B" is the stand-on vessel because she is to   starboard of vessel "A".

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel is "underway"  according to the Rules?
Option_A: A vessel made fast to a single point mooring buoy
Option_B: A purse seiner hauling her nets
Option_C: A pilot vessel at anchor
Option_D: A vessel which has run aground
Correct_Answer: A purse seiner hauling her nets

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When two power-driven vessels are crossing, the vessel which has the other to starboard must keep out of the way if _____.
Option_A: she is the faster vessel
Option_B: the situation involves risk of collision
Option_C: the vessels will pass within half a mile of each other
Correct_Answer: the situation involves risk of collision

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which signal may at some time be exhibited by a vessel trawling?
Option_A: Two white lights in a vertical line
Option_B: A white light over a red light in a vertical line
Option_C: Two red lights in a vertical line
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Risk of collision is considered to exist if _____.
Option_A: four vessels are nearby
Option_B: a vessel has a steady bearing at a constant range
Option_C: there is any doubt that a risk of collision exists
Option_D: a special circumstance situation is apparent
Correct_Answer: there is any doubt that a risk of collision exists

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway in low visibility and sounding fog signals. What changes would you make in the fog signal immediately upon losing propulsion?
Option_A: Begin sounding two prolonged blasts at two-minute intervals.
Option_B: Begin sounding one prolonged blast followed by three short blasts at two-minute intervals.
Option_C: Begin sounding one prolonged blast followed by two short blasts at two-minute intervals.
Option_D: No change should be made in the fog signal.
Correct_Answer: Begin sounding one prolonged blast followed by two short blasts at two-minute intervals.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel shows the same lights as a ___________________.
Option_A: vessel engaged in towing, when not underway
Option_B: vessel towing astern
Option_C: sailing vessel
Option_D: pushing vessel and a vessel being pushed, when they are  rigidly connected in a composite unit
Correct_Answer: pushing vessel and a vessel being pushed, when they are  rigidly connected in a composite unit

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel shall NOT show her sidelights?
Option_A: A fishing vessel that is not making way
Option_B: A sailing vessel which is becalmed
Option_C: A vessel engaged in underwater operations
Option_D: A vessel that is not under command making way
Correct_Answer: A fishing vessel that is not making way

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel is overtaking when§she can see which light(s) of a vessel ahead?
Option_A: Only the sternlight of the vessel
Option_B: One sidelight and a masthead light of the vessel
Option_C: Only a sidelight of the vessel
Option_D: The masthead lights of the vessel
Correct_Answer: Only the sternlight of the vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement about the Navigation Rules is TRUE?
Option_A: The rules require vessels to comply with Traffic Separation Scheme regulations.
Option_B: The rules use the term "safe speed."
Option_C: The Rules permit a stand-on vessel to take action prior to being in extremis.
Option_D: All of the above are correct.
Correct_Answer: All of the above are correct.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A "short blast" on the whistle has a duration of _________________.
Option_A: 1 second
Option_B: 4 to 6 seconds
Option_C: 8 to 12 seconds
Correct_Answer: 1 second

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND As defined in the Rules, the term "vessel" includes _____.
Option_A: seaplanes
Option_B: nondisplacement craft
Option_C: barges
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel shall slacken her speed, stop, or reverse her engines, if necessary, to_______________________.
Option_A: avoid collision
Option_B: allow more time to assess the situation
Option_C: be stopped in an appropriate distance
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND An anchor ball need NOT be exhibited by an anchored vessel if she is __________.
Option_A: under 50 meters in length, and anchored in an anchorage
Option_B: over 150 meters in length
Option_C: rigged for sail
Option_D: less than 7 meters in length, and not in or near an area where other vessels normally navigate
Correct_Answer: less than 7 meters in length, and not in or near an area where other vessels normally navigate

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL AND INLAND A vessel that is not equipped§with towing lights should show that it has a vessel in tow§by_________________.
Option_A: continuosly sounding its horn
Option_B: sounding one prolonged followed by two short blasts at intervals of not more than two minutes
Option_C: shining a searchlight on the towline of the towed vessel
Option_D: None of the above; a vessel shall not engage in towing at night without proper navigation lights
Correct_Answer: shining a searchlight on the towline of the towed vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway at night you are coming up on a vessel from astern. What lights would you expect to see?
Option_A: Red and green sidelights
Option_B: Two white lights
Option_C: One white light and red and green sidelights
Correct_Answer: One white light

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What describes a head-on  situation?
Option_A: Seeing one red light of a vessel directly ahead
Option_B: Seeing two forward white towing lights in a vertical line on a towing vessel directly ahead
Option_C: Seeing both sidelights of a vessel directly off your  starboard beam
Option_D: Seeing both sidelights of a vessel directly ahead
Correct_Answer: Seeing both sidelights of a vessel directly ahead

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel anchored in fog may warn an approaching vessel by sounding __________________.
Option_A: the whistle continuously
Option_B: one short, one prolonged, and one short blast of the  whistle
Option_C: five or more short and rapid blasts of the whistle
Option_D: three distinct strokes on the bell before and after sounding the anchor signal
Correct_Answer: one short, one prolonged, and one short blast of the  whistle

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway in fog, you hear a vessel ahead sound two prolonged blasts on the whistle. You should ______________________.
Option_A: sound two blasts and change course to the left
Option_B: sound whistle signals only if you change course
Option_C: sound only fog signals until the other vessel is sighted
Option_D: not sound any whistle signals until the other vessel is  sighted
Correct_Answer: sound only fog signals until the other vessel is sighted

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are operating in restricted visibility and hear a signal of a rapidly ringing bell  followed by the rapid sounding of a gong. It could be a  _________________.
Option_A: 30-meter sail vessel at anchor
Option_B: 150-meter power-driven vessel aground
Option_C: vessel in distress
Correct_Answer: 300-meter power-driven vessel at anchor

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel being towed, if manned, shall sound a fog signal of _____________________.
Option_A: two short blasts
Option_B: three short blasts
Option_C: one prolonged and two short blasts
Option_D: one prolonged and three short blasts
Correct_Answer: one prolonged and three short blasts

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel using a traffic  separation scheme shall _________.
Option_A: only anchor in the separation zone
Option_B: cross a traffic lane at as small an angle as possible
Option_C: avoid anchoring in areas near the termination of the scheme
Option_D: utilize the separation zone for navigating through the  scheme if she is impeding other traffic due to her slower speed
Correct_Answer: avoid anchoring in areas near the termination of the scheme

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A proper look-out shall be maintained _________________.
Option_A: only at night
Option_B: only during restricted visibility
Option_C: at night and during restricted visibility
Correct_Answer: at all times

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Risk of collision may be deemed to exist _____.
Option_A: if the compass bearing of an approaching vessel does NOT appreciably change
Option_B: even when an appreciable bearing change is evident,   particularly when approaching a vessel at close range
Option_C: if you observe both sidelights of a vessel ahead for an  extended period of time
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The Rules state that certain factors are to be taken into account when determining safe speed. Those factors include ______________________.
Option_A: state of wind, sea, and current, and the proximity of  navigational hazards
Option_B: maximum attainable speed of your vessel
Option_C: temperature
Option_D: aids to navigation that are available
