Correct_Answer: state of wind, sea, and current, and the proximity of  navigational hazards

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel, when anchored at night, would NOT be required to show anchor lights?
Option_A: A power-driven vessel
Option_B: A vessel on pilotage duty
Option_C: A vessel dredging
Option_D: A vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver
Correct_Answer: A vessel dredging

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel not under command shall display ____________________.
Option_A: two red lights at night and two black balls during daylight
Option_B: two red lights at night and three black balls during  daylight
Option_C: three red lights at night and two black balls during  daylight
Option_D: three red lights at night and three black balls during  daylight
Correct_Answer: two red lights at night and two black balls during daylight

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel engaged in fishing  while at anchor shall sound a fog signal of _____.
Option_A: one prolonged and two short blasts at two-minute intervals
Option_B: one prolonged and three short blasts at two-minute   intervals
Option_C: a rapid ringing of the bell for five seconds at one-minute intervals
Option_D: a sounding of the bell and gong at one-minute intervals
Correct_Answer: one prolonged and two short blasts at two-minute intervals

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Underway at night you see the red sidelight of a vessel well off your port bow. Which statement is TRUE?
Option_A: You are required to alter course to the right.
Option_B: You must stop engines.
Option_C: You are on a collision course with the other vessel.
Option_D: You may maintain course and speed.
Correct_Answer: You may maintain course and speed.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel would sound a fog signal consisting of the ringing of a bell for 5 seconds?
Option_A: A vessel engaged in fishing, at anchor
Option_B: A vessel restricted in its ability to maneuver, at anchor
Option_C: A sailing vessel, at anchor
Correct_Answer: A sailing vessel, at anchor

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel towing a barge astern would show, at the stern ___________________.
Option_A: only a sternlight
Option_B: a towing light above the sternlight
Option_C: two towing lights in a vertical line
Option_D: two white lights in a vertical line
Correct_Answer: a towing light above the sternlight

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A fog signal consisting of one prolonged blast followed by four short blasts would indicate the presence of a ___________________.
Option_A: vessel being towed
Option_B: fishing vessel engaged in trawling
Option_C: vessel at anchor warning of her location
Option_D: power-driven pilot vessel on station underway
Correct_Answer: power-driven pilot vessel on station underway

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In addition to sidelights what light should a vessel being towed astern show?
Option_A: A sternlight
Option_B: A masthead light
Option_C: Not under command lights
Correct_Answer: A sternlight

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A pilot vessel may continue to sound an identity signal if she is ___________________.
Option_A: aground
Option_B: at anchor
Option_C: not under command
Correct_Answer: at anchor

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When two power-driven vessels are meeting head-on and there is a risk of collision, each shall _______________.
Option_A: stop her engines
Option_B: alter course to starboard
Option_C: sound the danger signal
Correct_Answer: alter course to starboard

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power driven vessel when§towing and the length of the tow exceeds 200 meters shall§exhibit during daylight hours where they can best be§seen which of the following shapes?
Option_A: a diamond shape
Option_B: two cones, apexes together
Option_C: a black ball
Correct_Answer: a diamond shape

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is the minimum length of vessels required to show two anchor lights?
Option_A: 40 meters
Option_B: 50 meters
Option_C: 60 meters
Correct_Answer: 50 meters

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel showing a rigid replica of the International Code flag "A" is engaged in __________.
Option_A: diving operations
Option_B: dredging
Option_C: fishing
Correct_Answer: diving operations

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In determining "safe speed", all of the following must be taken into account EXCEPT the  _______________.
Option_A: maximum horsepower of your vessel
Option_B: presence of background lights at night
Option_C: draft of your vessel
Correct_Answer: maximum horsepower of your vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are aboard the give-way  vessel in a crossing situation. What should you NOT do in obeying the Rules?
Option_A: Cross ahead of the stand-on vessel
Option_B: Make a large course change to starboard
Option_C: Slow your vessel
Correct_Answer: Cross ahead of the stand-on vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel, which does not  normally engage in towing operations, is towing a vessel in distress. She ___________________.
Option_A: need not show the lights for a vessel engaged in towing, if it is impractical to do so
Option_B: may show the lights for a vessel not under command
Option_C: must show a yellow light above the sternlight
Option_D: must show the lights for a vessel towing
Correct_Answer: need not show the lights for a vessel engaged in towing, if it is impractical to do so

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND An all-round flashing yellow light may be exhibited by a(n) __________________.
Option_A: vessel laying cable
Option_B: vessel towing a submerged object
Option_C: vessel not under command
Correct_Answer: air cushion vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Working lights shall be used to illuminate the decks of a vessel ___________________.
Option_A: over 100 meters at anchor
Option_B: not under command
Option_C: constrained by her draft
Correct_Answer: over 100 meters at anchor

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel may show   identifying lights when not actually engaged in her   occupation?
Option_A: A fishing vessel
Option_B: A pilot vessel
Option_C: A mineclearance vessel
Correct_Answer: None of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A pilot vessel may continue to sound an identity signal if she is ___________________.
Option_A: underway, but not making way
Option_B: aground
Option_C: being towed
Correct_Answer: underway, but not making way

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If your vessel is the stand-on vessel in a crossing situation _____.
Option_A: you must keep your course and speed
Option_B: you may change course and speed as the other vessel must keep clear
Option_C: the other vessel must keep her course and speed
Option_D: both vessels must keep their course and speed
Correct_Answer: you must keep your course and speed

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel proceeding along a  narrow channel shall _____.
Option_A: avoid crossing the channel at right angles
Option_B: not overtake any vessels within the channel
Option_C: keep as near as safe and practicable to the limit of the channel on her starboard side
Option_D: when nearing a bend in the channel, sound a long blast of the whistle
Correct_Answer: keep as near as safe and practicable to the limit of the channel on her starboard side

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel would exhibit  sidelights when underway and not making way?
Option_A: A vessel towing astern
Option_B: A vessel trawling
Option_C: A vessel not under command
Option_D: A vessel engaged in dredging operations
Correct_Answer: A vessel towing astern

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel is NOT to impede the passage of a vessel which can only navigate safely  within a narrow channel?
Option_A: Any vessel less than 20 meters in length
Option_B: Any sailing vessel
Option_C: A vessel engaged in fishing
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A tug is towing three   manned barges in line in fog. The second vessel of the tow should sound ______________________.
Option_A: no fog signal
Option_B: one short blast
Option_C: one prolonged and three short blasts
Option_D: one prolonged and two short blasts
Correct_Answer: no fog signal

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The steering and sailing rules for vessels in restricted visibility apply to vessels _____.
Option_A: in sight of one another in fog
Option_B: navigating in or near an area of restricted visibility
Option_C: only if they are showing special purpose lights
Option_D: only if they have operational radar
Correct_Answer: navigating in or near an area of restricted visibility

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The Navigation Rules state that a vessel shall be operated at a safe speed at all times so that she can be stopped within _____.
Option_A: the distance of visibility
Option_B: 1/2 the distance of visibility
Option_C: a distance appropriate to the existing circumstances and conditions
Option_D: the distance that it would require for the propeller to go from full ahead to full astern
Correct_Answer: a distance appropriate to the existing circumstances and conditions

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A towing vessel 35 meters in length, with a tow 100 meters astern, must show a minimum of how many masthead lights?
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What must be TRUE in order for a stand-on vessel to take action to avoid collision by her maneuver alone?
Option_A: She must be in sight of the give-way vessel.
Option_B: There must be risk of collision.
Option_C: She must determine that the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action.
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel being towed astern, where the length of the tow exceeds 200 meters, will exhibit _________________.
Option_A: two balls in a vertical line
Option_B: a diamond shape where it can best be seen
Option_C: a ball on each end of the tow
Correct_Answer: a diamond shape where it can best be seen

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND For a stand-on vessel to take action to avoid collision she shall, if possible, NOT  _______.
Option_A: decrease speed
Option_B: increase speed
Option_C: turn to port for a vessel on her port side
Option_D: turn to starboard for a vessel on her port side
Correct_Answer: turn to port for a vessel on her port side

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You hear the fog signal of  another vessel forward of your beam. Risk of collision may exist. You MUST __________.
Option_A: reduce speed to bare steerageway
Option_B: stop your engines
Option_C: begin a radar plot
Correct_Answer: reduce speed to bare steerageway

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Two barges are being pushed  ahead by a tugboat. Which statement is TRUE concerning  lights on the barges?
Option_A: Each vessel should show sidelights.
Option_B: Each vessel should show at least one white light.
Option_C: The barges should be lighted as separate units.
Option_D: The barges should be lighted as one vessel.
Correct_Answer: The barges should be lighted as one vessel.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The Rules state that a seaplane shall _____________________.
Option_A: not be regarded as a vessel
Option_B: in general, keep well clear of all vessels
Option_C: proceed at a slower speed than surrounding vessels
Option_D: when making way, show the lights for a vessel not under  command
Correct_Answer: in general, keep well clear of all vessels

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If practical, when shall a  manned vessel being towed sound her fog signal?
Option_A: Immediately before the towing vessel sounds hers
Option_B: Immediately after the towing vessel sounds hers
Option_C: As close to the mid-cycle of the towing vessel's signals as possible
Option_D: At any time as long as the interval is correct
Correct_Answer: Immediately after the towing vessel sounds hers

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your tug is underway at night and NOT towing. What light(s) should your vessel show aft to other vessels coming up from astern?
Option_A: One white light
Option_B: Two white lights
Option_C: One white light and one yellow light
Option_D: One white light and two yellow lights
Correct_Answer: One white light

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel conducting mineclearing operations will show _________________.
Option_A: three balls in a vertical line
Option_B: two balls in a vertical line
Option_C: one ball near the foremast and one ball at each fore yard
Option_D: one diamond near the foremast head and one ball at each  fore yard
Correct_Answer: one ball near the foremast and one ball at each fore yard

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel sailing shall keep out of the way of all of the following vessels except a vessel ___________________.
Option_A: not under command
Option_B: engaged on pilotage duty
Option_C: restricted in her ability to maneuver
Correct_Answer: engaged on pilotage duty

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning a vessel under oars?
Option_A: She must show a sternlight.
Option_B: She is allowed to show the same lights as a sailing vessel.
Option_C: She must show a fixed all-round white light.
Option_D: She must show a dayshape of a black cone.
Correct_Answer: She is allowed to show the same lights as a sailing vessel.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel is  underway and fishing with trolling lines. This vessel  _____________________.
Option_A: must keep out of the way of sailing vessels
Option_B: must sound a one prolonged, two short blasts signal in  restricted visibility
Option_C: is the stand-on vessel when overtaking power-driven vessels
Correct_Answer: must keep out of the way of sailing vessels

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND At night you sight a vessel  displaying a single green light. This is a _____.
Option_A: vessel at anchor
Option_B: small motorboat underway
Option_C: vessel drifting
Correct_Answer: sailing vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When two power-driven vessels are crossing, which vessel is the stand-on vessel?
Option_A: The vessel which is to starboard of the other vessel
Option_B: The vessel which is to port of the other vessel
Option_C: The larger vessel
Option_D: The vessel that sounds the first whistle signal
Correct_Answer: The vessel which is to starboard of the other vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel must exhibit forward and after white masthead lights when making way?
Option_A: A 75-meter vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver
Option_B: A 100-meter sailing vessel
Option_C: A 150-meter vessel engaged in fishing
Correct_Answer: A 75-meter vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND By radar alone, you detect a§vessel ahead on a collision course, about 3 miles distant.§ Your radar plot shows this to be a meeting situation. You§should _______.
Option_A: turn to port
Option_B: turn to starboard
Option_C: maintain course and speed and sound the danger signal
Option_D: maintain course and speed and sound no signal
Correct_Answer: turn to starboard

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A sailing vessel underway at night may show _________________.
Option_A: a red light over a green light at the masthead
Option_B: a green light over a red light at the masthead
Option_C: two white lights in a vertical line at the stern
Option_D: an all-round white light at the bow
Correct_Answer: a red light over a green light at the masthead

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel engaged in trawling will show identification lights of ___________________.
Option_A: a red light over a white light
Option_B: a white light over a red light
Option_C: a green light over a white light
Option_D: two red lights in a vertical line
Correct_Answer: a green light over a white light

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is required of a vessel§navigating near an area of restricted visibility?
Option_A: A power-driven vessel shall have her engines ready for  immediate maneuver.
Option_B: She must sound appropriate sound signals.
Option_C: If she detects another vessel by radar, she shall determine if risk of collision exists.
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND By night, you sight the lights of a vessel engaged in underwater operations. If an   obstruction exists on the port side of the vessel, it will be marked by _________________.
Option_A: a floodlight
Option_B: two red lights in a vertical line
Option_C: a single red light
Correct_Answer: two red lights in a vertical line

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel may carry her  sidelights and sternlight in one combined lantern?
Option_A: A 10-meter power-driven vessel
Option_B: A 15-meter vessel propelled by sail and machinery
Option_C: A 10-meter sailing vessel
Correct_Answer: A 10-meter sailing vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which lights would be shown at night by a vessel which is restricted in her ability to  deviate from her course?
Option_A: Three red lights in a vertical line
Option_B: Three white lights in a vertical line
Option_C: Three lights in a vertical line, the highest and lowest  white and the middle red
Option_D: Three lights in a vertical line, the highest and lowest red and the middle white
Correct_Answer: Three lights in a vertical line, the highest and lowest red and the middle white

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel is the stand-on vessel when two vessels crossing in fog are NOT in sight of one another?
Option_A: The vessel which has the other on her own starboard side
Option_B: The vessel which has the other on her own port side
Option_C: The one which hears the other's fog signal first
Option_D: Neither vessel is the stand-on vessel.
Correct_Answer: Neither vessel is the stand-on vessel.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel engaged in fishing  shall keep out of the way of a vessel _____.
Option_A: under sail
Option_B: restricted in her ability to maneuver
Option_C: crossing a channel
Correct_Answer: restricted in her ability to maneuver

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessels shall turn off their sidelights?
Option_A: All vessels that are not under command
Option_B: All fishing vessels that are not making way
Option_C: All sailing vessels which are becalmed
Option_D: All vessels engaged in underwater operations
Correct_Answer: All fishing vessels that are not making way

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel fishing at night, with gear extending more than 150 meters horizontally outwards, will show in the direction of the gear _________________.
Option_A: one white light
Option_B: two vertical white lights
Option_C: one yellow light
Correct_Answer: one white light

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In restricted visibility, a  vessel which detects by radar alone the presence of another vessel shall determine if a close quarters situation is  developing or risk of collision exists. If so, she shall _____.
Option_A: sound the danger signal
Option_B: when taking action, make only course changes
Option_C: avoid altering course toward a vessel abaft the beam
Correct_Answer: avoid altering course toward a vessel abaft the beam

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 60-meter vessel which is  trawling is required to show how many white masthead lights at night?
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel servicing a pipeline during the day shall display ___________________.
Option_A: three black shapes in a vertical line; the highest and  lowest are balls, and the middle one is a diamond
Option_B: three shapes in a vertical line; the highest and lowest are red balls, and the middle one is a white diamond
Option_C: three black balls in a vertical line
Option_D: two black balls in a vertical line
Correct_Answer: three black shapes in a vertical line; the highest and  lowest are balls, and the middle one is a diamond

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In fog you observe your radar and determine that risk of collision exists with a vessel which is 2 miles off your port bow. You should __________.
Option_A: stop your engines
Option_B: sound the danger signal at two-minute intervals
Option_C: hold course and speed until the other vessel is sighted
Option_D: take avoiding action as soon as possible
Correct_Answer: take avoiding action as soon as possible

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning a towing vessel which, due to the nature of her work, is unable to keep out of the way of another vessel?
Option_A: By day, she shall carry a black cylinder shape.
Option_B: By day, she shall carry two black balls in a vertical line.
Option_C: By night, she would show the same lights as a vessel not under command.
Option_D: By day, she would show the same shapes as a vessel   restricted in her ability to maneuver.
Correct_Answer: By day, she would show the same shapes as a vessel   restricted in her ability to maneuver.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   regarding equipment for bell & gong signals?
Option_A: A vessel of less than 12 meters in length need not have any sound signaling equipment.
Option_B: Manual sounding of the signals must always be possible.
Option_C: Any vessel over 12 meters in length must be provided with a gong.
Option_D: Signals must be able to be sounded manually and    automatically.
Correct_Answer: Manual sounding of the signals must always be possible.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are approaching a narrow channel. You see a vessel that can only be navigated safely within the channel. You MUST _____.
Option_A: hold your course and speed
Option_B: sound the danger signal
Option_C: not cross the channel if you might impede the other vessel
Option_D: initiate an exchange of passing signals
Correct_Answer: not cross the channel if you might impede the other vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is the minimum sound  signaling equipment required aboard a vessel 10 meters in length?
Option_A: Any means of making an efficient sound signal
Option_B: A bell only
Option_C: A whistle only
Correct_Answer: Any means of making an efficient sound signal

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel must have a gong, or other equipment which will make the sound of a gong?
Option_A: A sailing vessel
Option_B: Any vessel over 50 meters
Option_C: A power driven vessel over 75 meters
Correct_Answer: Any vessel over 100 meters

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway and in sight of another vessel, less than one half mile away, you put your engines on astern propulsion. Which statement concerning whistle signals is TRUE?
Option_A: You need not sound any whistle signals.
Option_B: You must sound one blast if backing to starboard.
Option_C: You must sound whistle signals only if the vessels are  meeting.
Option_D: You must sound three short blasts on the whistle.
Correct_Answer: You must sound three short blasts on the whistle.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE  concerning the light used with whistle signals?
Option_A: Use of such a light is required.
Option_B: Its purpose is to supplement short blasts of the whistle.
Option_C: The light shall have the same characteristics as a masthead light.
Correct_Answer: Its purpose is to supplement short blasts of the whistle.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What determines if a vessel is "restricted in her ability to maneuver"?
Option_A: Whether or not all of the vessel's control equipment is in working order
Option_B: The vessel's draft in relation to the available depth of water
Option_C: Whether the nature of the vessel's work limits    maneuverability required by the Rules
Option_D: Whether or not the vessel is the give-way vessel in a  meeting situation
Correct_Answer: Whether the nature of the vessel's work limits    maneuverability required by the Rules

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is true   concerning the light used to accompany whistle signals?
Option_A: It is only used to supplement short blasts of the whistle.
Option_B: It is mandatory to use such a light.

Option_B: maximum speed of your vessel
Option_C: temperature
Correct_Answer: current

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND "Safe speed" is defined as that speed where _____.
Option_A: you can stop within your visibility range
Option_B: the vessel is not subject to vibrations
Option_C: you are travelling slower than surrounding vessels
Option_D: you can take proper and effective action to avoid   collision
Correct_Answer: you can take proper and effective action to avoid   collision

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The Rules state that risk of collision shall be deemed to exist _____.
Option_A: whenever two vessels are on opposite courses
Option_B: whenever a vessel crosses ahead of the intended track of another vessel
Option_C: if the bearing of an approaching vessel does not   appreciably change
Option_D: if one vessel approaches another so as to be    overtaking
Correct_Answer: if the bearing of an approaching vessel does not   appreciably change

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND. In which situation would you consider a risk of collision to exist?
Option_A: A vessel is one point on your starboard bow, range   increasing, bearing changing slightly to the right.
Option_B: A vessel is broad on your starboard beam, range decreasing, bearing changing rapidly to the right.
Option_C: A vessel is two points abaft your port beam, range   decreasing, bearing constant.
Option_D: A vessel is on your starboard quarter, range increasing, bearing is constant.
Correct_Answer: A vessel is two points abaft your port beam, range   decreasing, bearing constant.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is TRUE when operating in fog and other vessels are detected by radar?
Option_A: You should make an ample change to port for a vessel crossing on the starboard bow.
Option_B: You should maneuver in ample time if a close-quarters situation is developing.
Option_C: You should determine the course and speed of all radar  contacts at six minute intervals.
Option_D: Long-range scanning will provide early warning of ALL other vessels within the radar's range.
Correct_Answer: You should maneuver in ample time if a close-quarters situation is developing.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are approaching another  vessel on crossing courses. She is about one mile distant and is on your starboard bow. You believe she will cross ahead of you but she sounds a whistle signal of five short blasts. You should _____.
Option_A: answer the signal and hold course and speed
Option_B: reduce speed slightly
Option_C: initiate a passing signal that will allow for a    half mile clearance
Option_D: make a large course change, and slow down if necessary
Correct_Answer: make a large course change, and slow down if necessary

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are approaching another  vessel on crossing courses. She is approximately half a mile distant on your starboard bow. You believe she will cross ahead of you but she sounds a whistle signal of five short blasts. You should __________.
Option_A: sound a signal of one prolonged blast
Option_B: make a large course change
Option_C: reduce speed slightly to make sure she will have room  to pass
Option_D: wait for another whistle signal from the other vessel
Correct_Answer: make a large course change

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Under the Rules, any vessel may slacken her speed, stop, or reverse her engines to   __________.
Option_A: create a crossing situation
Option_B: allow more time to assess the situation
Option_C: attract the attention of another vessel
Correct_Answer: allow more time to assess the situation

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When in sight of another§vessel, any action taken to avoid collision must _________.
Option_A: be accompanied by sound signals
Option_B: not result in another close quarters situation
Option_C: include a speed change
Correct_Answer: not result in another close quarters situation

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel approaching a narrow channel shall _____.
Option_A: avoid crossing the channel if it impedes another vessel  navigating in the channel
Option_B: not overtake any vessels within the channel
Option_C: keep as close as possible to the edge of the channel on  her port side
Option_D: anchor only in the middle of the channel
Correct_Answer: avoid crossing the channel if it impedes another vessel  navigating in the channel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When underway in a channel, you should _____.
Option_A: stay near the middle of the channel
Option_B: keep to the starboard side of any vessels you meet
Option_C: exchange whistle signals with any other vessels in the  channel
Option_D: keep to the side of the channel which lies to your starboard
Correct_Answer: keep to the side of the channel which lies to your starboard

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A sailing vessel is proceeding along a narrow channel and can safely navigate ONLY inside the channel. The sailing vessel approaches a vessel engaged in fishing in the narrow channel. Which statement is TRUE?
Option_A: Each vessel should move to the edge of the channel on  her port side.
Option_B: The vessels are required to exchange signals.
Option_C: The fishing vessel is directed not to impede the   passage of the sailing vessel.
Option_D: Each vessel should be displaying signals for a vessel  constrained by her draft.
Correct_Answer: The fishing vessel is directed not to impede the   passage of the sailing vessel.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL AND INLAND A vessel engaged in   mineclearance operations shows special identity lights ____.
Option_A: in addition to the lights required for a power-driven vessel
Option_B: which means that other vessels should not approach closer than 500 meters on either side of the vessel
Option_C: that are green and show through an arc of the horizon of 225°
Correct_Answer: in addition to the lights required for a power-driven vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When navigating in thick fog with the radar on, you should _________________.
Option_A: station the look-out in the wheelhouse to keep a continuous watch on the radar
Option_B: secure the sounding of fog signals until a vessel closes within five miles
Option_C: station a look-out as low down and far forward as possible
Option_D: keep the radar on the shortest available range for early detection of approaching vessels
Correct_Answer: station a look-out as low down and far forward as possible

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL AND INLAND You are underway in thick§fog. You have not determined if risk of collision exists. §Which statement is TRUE?
Option_A: Your speed must be reduced to bare steerageway.
Option_B: A look-out is not required if the radar is on.
Option_C: Fog signals are only required when a vessel is detected by radar.
Option_D: The radar should always be kept on a short-range scale.
Correct_Answer: Your speed must be reduced to bare steerageway.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A sailing vessel is proceeding along a narrow channel and can safely navigate ONLY inside the channel. The sailing vessel approaches a vessel engaged in fishing. Which statement is TRUE?
Option_A: The fishing vessel must sound the danger signal.
Option_B: The fishing vessel shall not impede the passage of the  sailing vessel.
Option_C: Each vessel should move to the edge of the channel on her port side.
Option_D: Both vessels should be displaying the signal for a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver.
Correct_Answer: The fishing vessel shall not impede the passage of the  sailing vessel.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL AND INLAND Which vessel shall NOT§impede the passage of a vessel which can safely navigate§only within a narrow channel or fairway?
Option_A: A vessel dredging
Option_B: A sailing vessel
Option_C: A vessel servicing an aid to navigation
Correct_Answer: A sailing vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your 15-meter vessel is  crossing a narrow channel and a large cargo vessel to  starboard is within the channel and crossing your course. You should _________.
Option_A: hold your course and speed
Option_B: sound the danger signal
Option_C: keep out of the way of the cargo vessel
Correct_Answer: keep out of the way of the cargo vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If two sailing vessels are  running free with the wind on the same side, which one must keep clear of the other?
Option_A: The one with the wind closest abeam
Option_B: The one to windward
Option_C: The one to leeward
Option_D: The one that sounds the first whistle signal
Correct_Answer: The one to windward

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE  concerning two sailing vessels approaching each other?
Option_A: The vessel making the most speed is the give-way vessel.
Option_B: A sailing vessel overtaking another is the give-way vessel.
Option_C: A sailing vessel seeing another to leeward on an   undetermined tack shall hold her course.
Correct_Answer: A sailing vessel overtaking another is the give-way vessel.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Power-driven vessels must keep out of the way of sailing vessels except ___________.
Option_A: in a crossing situation
Option_B: when they are making more speed than the power-driven  vessel
Option_C: when the sailing vessel is overtaking
Option_D: on the Inland Waters of the United States
Correct_Answer: when the sailing vessel is overtaking

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When do the Rules require both vessels to change course?
Option_A: Any time the danger signal is sounded
Option_B: When two power-driven vessels are crossing and it is  apparent to the stand-on vessel that the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action
Option_C: When two power-driven vessels are meeting head-on
Correct_Answer: When two power-driven vessels are meeting head-on

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your vessel is NOT making way, but is not in any way disabled. Another vessel is   approaching you on your starboard beam. Which statement is TRUE?
Option_A: Your vessel is obligated to stay out of the way.
Option_B: The other vessel must give way, since your vessel is  stopped.
Option_C: You should be showing the lights or shapes for a vessel not under command.
Option_D: You should be showing the lights or shapes for a vessel  restricted in her ability to maneuver.
Correct_Answer: Your vessel is obligated to stay out of the way.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If you are the stand-on vessel in a crossing situation, you may take action to avoid  collision by your maneuver alone. When may this action be taken?
Option_A: As soon as you determine that risk of collision exists
Option_B: Only when you have reached extremis
Option_C: When it becomes apparent to you that the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action
Option_D: When you determine that your present course will cross ahead of the other vessel
Correct_Answer: When it becomes apparent to you that the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In a crossing situation on§open waters, a sailing vessel shall keep out of the way of§all the following vessels EXCEPT a vessel _____.
Option_A: not under command
Option_B: restricted in her ability to maneuver
Option_C: engaged in towing
Correct_Answer: engaged in towing

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What would be a "special  circumstance" under the Rules?
Option_A: Vessel at anchor
Option_B: Two vessels meeting
Option_C: Speed in fog
Correct_Answer: More than two vessels crossing

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In restricted visibility, a  vessel being towed, if manned, shall sound a signal of ____.
Option_A: one prolonged and three short blasts
Option_B: one prolonged and two short blasts
Option_C: three short blasts
Correct_Answer: one prolonged and three short blasts

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are approaching a narrow§channel. Another vessel in the channel can only be§navigated safely in that channel. You should _____________.
Option_A: sound two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast
Option_B: not cross the channel if you might impede the other vessel
Option_C: sound three short blasts, and take all way off your vessel
Option_D: hold your course and speed if he is on your port bow
Correct_Answer: not cross the channel if you might impede the other vessel

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are the stand-on vessel in a crossing situation. If you think the give-way vessel is NOT taking sufficient action to avoid collision, you should sound _____________________.
Option_A: one short blast and maintain course
Option_B: two short blasts, alter to port, and pass astern
Option_C: the danger signal
Option_D: no signal and maneuver at will
Correct_Answer: the danger signal

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway in fog, you hear a vessel ahead sound two prolonged blasts on the whistle. You should _____.
Option_A: sound only fog signals until the other vessel is sighted
Option_B: not sound any whistle signals until the other vessel is  sighted
Option_C: sound two blasts and change course to the left
Option_D: sound whistle signals only if you change course
Correct_Answer: sound only fog signals until the other vessel is sighted

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Lighting requirements in§inland waters are different from those for international§waters for _____.
Option_A: barges being towed astern
Option_B: vessels not under command
Option_C: vessels pushing ahead
Correct_Answer: vessels pushing ahead

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND There are two classes of vessels which do not have to comply with the rule regarding traffic separation schemes, to the extent necessary to carry out their work. One of those is a vessel _______________.
Option_A: engaged in fishing
Option_B: towing another
Option_C: servicing a navigational aid
Correct_Answer: servicing a navigational aid

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In a traffic separation scheme, when joining a traffic lane from the side, a vessel shall do so _____________.
Option_A: only in case of an emergency or to engage in fishing within the zone
Option_B: as nearly as practical at right angles to the general  direction of traffic flow
Option_C: at as small an angle as possible
Option_D: only to anchor within the zone
Correct_Answer: at as small an angle as possible

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A traffic separation zone is that part of a traffic separation scheme which __________.
Option_A: is located between the scheme and the nearest land
Option_B: separates traffic proceeding in one direction from traffic proceeding in the opposite direction
Option_C: is designated as an anchorage area
Option_D: contains all the traffic moving in the same direction
Correct_Answer: separates traffic proceeding in one direction from traffic proceeding in the opposite direction

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel using a traffic  separation scheme shall _______________.
Option_A: avoid anchoring in areas near the termination of the scheme
Option_B: avoid crossing traffic lanes, but if obliged to do so, shall cross on as small an angle as is practical
Option_C: only anchor in the separation zone
Option_D: use the separation zone for navigating through the scheme if she is hindering other traffic due to her slower speed
Correct_Answer: avoid anchoring in areas near the termination of the scheme

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel using a traffic  separation scheme shall NOT _____________.
Option_A: cross a traffic lane
Option_B: engage in fishing the separation zone
Option_C: proceed in an inappropriate traffic lane
Correct_Answer: proceed in an inappropriate traffic lane

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel using a traffic  separation scheme shall _____.
Option_A: only anchor in the separation zone
Option_B: avoid crossing traffic lanes, but if obliged to do so, shall cross on a heading at as small an angle as is practical
Option_C: avoid anchoring in areas near the termination of the scheme
Option_D: use the separation zone for navigation through the scheme if she is hindering other traffic due to her slower speed
Correct_Answer: avoid anchoring in areas near the termination of the scheme

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway in fog, you hear a vessel ahead sound two prolonged blasts on the whistle. You should _______________________.
Option_A: sound two blasts and change course to the left
Option_B: sound only fog signals until the other vessel is sighted
Option_C: sound whistle signals only if you change course
Option_D: not sound any whistle signals until the other vessel is  sighted
Correct_Answer: sound only fog signals until the other vessel is sighted

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A towing vessel and her tow are severely restricted in their ability to change course. §When making way, the towing vessel will show ONLY _____.
Option_A: the masthead lights for a towing vessel
Option_B: the lights for a vessel restricted in her ability to  maneuver
Option_C: sidelights,stern light, and towing light
Correct_Answer: All of the above.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You hear the fog signal of  another vessel forward of your beam. Risk of collision may exist. You MUST __________.
Option_A: take all way off, if necessary
Option_B: stop your engines
Option_C: begin a radar plot
Correct_Answer: take all way off, if necessary

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A fog signal of one short, one prolonged, and one short blast may be sounded by a _____.
Option_A: vessel not under command
Option_B: vessel at anchor
Option_C: vessel towing
Correct_Answer: vessel at anchor

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You hear the fog signal of  another vessel forward of your beam. Risk of collision may exist. You MUST _____.
Option_A: stop your engines
Option_B: take all way off, if necessary
Option_C: begin a radar plot
Correct_Answer: take all way off, if necessary

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel may enter a traffic separation zone ___________.
Option_A: in an emergency
Option_B: to engage in fishing within the zone
Option_C: to cross the traffic separation scheme
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In a traffic separation scheme, when joining a traffic lane from the side, a vessel shall do so _______________.
Option_A: at as small an angle as possible
Option_B: as nearly as practical at right angles to the general  direction of traffic flow
Option_C: only in case of an emergency or to engage in fishing within the zone
Correct_Answer: at as small an angle as possible

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel using a traffic  separation scheme is forbidden to _________________.
Option_A: proceed through an inappropriate traffic lane
Option_B: engaged in fishing in the separation zone
Option_C: cross a traffic lane
Option_D: enter the separation zone, even in a emergency
Correct_Answer: proceed through an inappropriate traffic lane

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A traffic separation zone is that part of a traffic separation scheme which ________.
Option_A: is between the scheme and the nearest land
Option_B: contains all the traffic moving in one direction
Option_C: is designated as an anchorage area
Option_D: separates traffic proceeding in one direction from traffic proceeding in the opposite direction
Correct_Answer: separates traffic proceeding in one direction from traffic proceeding in the opposite direction

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY To indicate that a vessel is constrained by her draft, a vessel may display, in a vertical line,  ____________.
Option_A: three 360° red lights
Option_B: two 225° red lights
Option_C: three 360° blue lights
Correct_Answer: three 360° red lights

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY A power-driven vessel pushing ahead§or towing alongside displays navigation lights and _____.
Option_A: two all-round red lights in a vertical line
Option_B: two yellow towing lights in a vertical line
Option_C: two white masthead lights in a vertical line
Option_D: two lights on the stern, one yellow and one white
Correct_Answer: two white masthead lights in a vertical line

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which statement is true concerning a  vessel "constrained by her draft"?
Option_A: She must be a power-driven vessel.
Option_B: She is not under command.
Option_C: She may be a vessel being towed.
Option_D: She is hampered because of her work.
Correct_Answer: She must be a power-driven vessel.

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY When moving from a berth alongside a quay (wharf), a vessel must sound _____.
Option_A: three short blasts
Option_B: a long blast
Option_C: a prolonged blast
Correct_Answer: No signal is required.

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY You are in charge of a 250-meter freight vessel constrained by her draft proceeding down a narrow channel. There is a vessel engaged in fishing on your starboard bow half a mile away. §According to Rule 9, which statement is TRUE?
Option_A: You are not to impede the fishing vessel.
Option_B: If you are in doubt as to the fishing vessel's intentions you may sound at least five short and rapid blasts on the whistle.
Option_C: You are to slow to bare steerageway until clear of the  fishing vessel.
Option_D: You must sound one prolonged blast to alert the fishing vessel.
Correct_Answer: If you are in doubt as to the fishing vessel's intentions you may sound at least five short and rapid blasts on the whistle.

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY The International Rules of the Road apply _______________________.
Option_A: to all waters which are not inland waters
Option_B: only to waters outside the territorial waters of the United States
Option_C: only to waters where foreign vessels travel
Option_D: upon the high seas and connecting waters navigable by  seagoing vessels
Correct_Answer: upon the high seas and connecting waters navigable by  seagoing vessels

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY A towing light is _____.
Option_A: shown at the bow
Option_B: white in color
Option_C: shown in addition to the sternlight
Correct_Answer: shown in addition to the sternlight

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY In a narrow channel, an overtaking vessel which intends to pass on the other vessel's port side would sound _____.
Option_A: one prolonged followed by two short blasts
Option_B: one short blast
Option_C: two short blasts
Option_D: two prolonged followed by two short blasts
Correct_Answer: two prolonged followed by two short blasts

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY You are underway on the high seas in  restricted visibility. You hear a fog signal of one  prolonged and two short blasts. It could be any of the  following EXCEPT a vessel _____.
Option_A: minesweeping
Option_B: engaged in fishing
Option_C: constrained by her draft
Correct_Answer: being towed

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY A vessel displaying three red lights in a vertical line is ___________________.
Option_A: not under command
Option_B: aground
Option_C: dredging
Correct_Answer: constrained by her draft

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY At night, a power-driven vessel underway of less than 7 meters in length where its maximum speed does not exceed 7 knots may show, as a minimum, _____.
Option_A: sidelights and a sternlight
Option_B: the lights required for a vessel more than 7 meters in  length
Option_C: sidelights only
Correct_Answer: one all-round white light

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY In a narrow channel, a signal of intent which must be answered by the other vessel, is sounded by a vessel ____________________.
Option_A: meeting another head-on
Option_B: crossing the course of another
Option_C: overtaking another
Correct_Answer: overtaking another

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY When two vessels are in sight of one  another, all of the following signals may be given EXCEPT _____________________.
Option_A: a light signal of at least five short and rapid flashes
Option_B: four short whistle blasts
Option_C: one prolonged, one short, one prolonged and one short  whistle blasts
Correct_Answer: four short whistle blasts

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY A power-driven vessel leaving a quay or wharf must sound what signal?
Option_A: Three short blasts
Option_B: A long blast
Option_C: A prolonged blast
Correct_Answer: No signal is required.

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Lighting requirements in inland waters are different from those in international waters for _____.
Option_A: barges being pushed ahead
Option_B: vessels constrained by their draft
Option_C: vessels towing by pushing ahead
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY What whistle signal, if any, would be sounded when two vessels are meeting, but will pass clear starboard to starboard?
Option_A: One short blast
Option_B: Two short blasts
Option_C: Five or more short blasts
Correct_Answer: No signal is required.

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY In a narrow channel, a vessel trying to overtake another on the other vessel's port side, would  sound a whistle signal of _________________.
Option_A: one short blast
Option_B: two short blasts
Option_C: two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast
Option_D: two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts
Correct_Answer: two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY On open water, a power-driven vessel  coming up dead astern of another vessel and altering her course to starboard so as to pass on the starboard side of the vessel ahead would sound _____________.
Option_A: two short blasts
Option_B: one short blast
Option_C: two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast
Option_D: one long and one short blast
Correct_Answer: one short blast

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY If a vessel displays three all-round red lights in a vertical line at night, during the day she may show ___________.
Option_A: three balls in a vertical line
Option_B: a cylinder
Option_C: two diamonds in a vertical line
Correct_Answer: a cylinder

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY A vessel not under command sounds the same fog signal as a vessel _____.
Option_A: towing
Option_B: constrained by her draft
Option_C: under sail
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY Your vessel is crossing a narrow channel. A vessel to port is within the channel and crossing your course. She is showing a black cylinder. What is your  responsibility?
Option_A: Hold your course and speed.
Option_B: Sound the danger signal.
Option_C: Begin an exchange of passing signals.
Option_D: Do not cross the channel if you might impede the other  vessel.
Correct_Answer: Do not cross the channel if you might impede the other  vessel.

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY You are approaching another vessel and will pass starboard to starboard without danger if no course changes are made. You should ___________________.
Option_A: hold course and sound a two blast whistle signal
Option_B: hold course and sound no whistle signal
Option_C: change course to the right and sound one blast
Option_D: hold course and sound two prolonged and two short blasts
Correct_Answer: hold course and sound no whistle signal

Question_Text: BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A fishing vessel is approaching a vessel not under command. Which statement is TRUE?
Option_A: The fishing vessel must keep clear of the vessel not under command.
Option_B: If the vessel not under command is a power-driven vessel, she must keep clear of the fishing vessel.
Option_C: They must exchange whistle signals.
Option_D: Both vessels are required to take action to stay clear of each other.
Correct_Answer: The fishing vessel must keep clear of the vessel not under command.

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which signal is required to be sounded by a power driven vessel ONLY?
Option_A: A signal meaning, "I am altering my course to starboard."
Option_B: A signal meaning, "I intend to overtake you on your starboard side."
Option_C: A signal meaning that the vessel sounding it is in doubt as to the other vessel's actions.
Option_D: A signal sounded when approaching a bend.
Correct_Answer: A signal meaning, "I am altering my course to starboard."

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY The light which may be used with a  vessel's whistle is to be ___________________.
Option_A: used when the whistle is broken
Option_B: used prior to sounding the whistle
Option_C: used only at night
Correct_Answer: a white light

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY You are in sight of another vessel in a crossing situation, and the other vessel sounds one short blast. You are going to hold course and speed. You should _______________________.
Option_A: answer with one short blast
Option_B: answer with two short blasts
Option_C: sound the danger signal
Correct_Answer: sound no whistle signal

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY Two prolonged blasts followed by one  short blast on the whistle is a signal which could be  sounded by a _________________.
Option_A: fishing vessel
Option_B: vessel anchored
Option_C: mineclearing vessel
Option_D: vessel overtaking another in a narrow channel
Correct_Answer: vessel overtaking another in a narrow channel

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY In a crossing situation on international waters, a short blast by the give-way vessel indicates that the vessel ________.
Option_A: is holding course and speed
Option_B: is turning to starboard
Option_C: intends to pass port to port
Option_D: will keep out of the way of the stand-on vessel
Correct_Answer: is turning to starboard

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY What dayshape is prescribed for a vessel constrained by her draft?
Option_A: A black cone, apex upward
Option_B: A black cone, apex downward
Option_C: Two vertical black balls
Correct_Answer: A cylinder

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY A vessel not under command sounds the same fog signal as a vessel _____________________.
Option_A: engaged in towing
Option_B: constrained by her draft
Option_C: under sail
Correct_Answer: All of the above

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which statement(s) is(are) TRUE concerning light signals?
Option_A: The time between flashes shall be about five seconds.
Option_B: The time between successive signals shall be not less than ten seconds.
Option_C: The light signals are to be used when not using sound  signals.
Correct_Answer: The time between successive signals shall be not less than ten seconds.

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY Under what circumstances would an  overtaking vessel sound a whistle signal of two prolonged followed by one short blast?
Option_A: When overtaking in restricted visibility
Option_B: When overtaking in a narrow channel
Option_C: When overtaking on open waters
Option_D: When no other vessels are in the immediate area
Correct_Answer: When overtaking in a narrow channel

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY In which case would an overtaking vessel sound a whistle signal of two prolonged followed by one  short blast?
Option_A: When overtaking in restricted visibility
Option_B: When overtaking in a narrow channel
Option_C: When overtaking on open waters
Option_D: When no other vessels are in the immediate area
Correct_Answer: When overtaking in a narrow channel

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY When vessels are in sight of one another, two short blasts from one of the vessels means ____________.
Option_A: "I am altering my course to starboard"
Option_B: "I am altering my course to port"
Option_C: "I intend to change course to starboard"
Option_D: "I intend to change course to port"
Correct_Answer: "I am altering my course to port"

Question_Text: INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which vessel may NOT exhibit two red  lights in a vertical line?
Option_A: A vessel constrained by her draft
Option_B: A trawler fishing in close proximity to other trawlers
Option_C: A vessel aground
Correct_Answer: A vessel constrained by her draft
